  • Appling Tax Commissioner official site/URL, due dates, penalties not located

Which Appling County offices handle a tax bill?

Two neighboring suites in the Courthouse Annex on Tippins Street in Baxley divide the job. Suite 101 is the Board of Tax Assessors, which decides what your land and house are worth. Suite 102 is the Tax Commissioner, which mails the bill and takes your money.

Calling the wrong door wastes a day, so match the question to the office. Anything about a value, a mistake in the property record, an exemption or an appeal belongs with the assessors. Anything about the amount owed, a payment method or an old balance belongs with the tax commissioner. Property records can be searched at qpublic.net/ga/appling, and the tax commissioner's page points to an online payment portal.

Appling County offices a seller may need (source: county staff directory and tax commissioner page)
OfficeLocationPhone
Board of Tax Assessors69 Tippins Street, Suite 101, Baxley(912) 367-8108
Tax Commissioner69 Tippins Street, Suite 102, Baxley(912) 367-8105
Clerk of Courts69 Tippins Street, Suite 103, Baxley(912) 367-8126
Probate Court36 South Main Street, Baxley(912) 367-8114

The tax commissioner's counter is open weekdays, with a morning start at 8 and a close at 5. Liens against a parcel are recorded through the clerk, so Suite 103 matters when a county claim is attached to a house headed to market.

Where does Appling County sit, and who lives in it?

Appling County has roughly 507 square miles of land area in southeast Georgia, and Baxley, the county seat, is also the largest town. Graham and Surrency are the two other incorporated places, and Holmesville is the old courthouse community that lost the seat to Baxley after an 1872 vote tied to the Macon and Brunswick Railroad.

Census estimates put the county at 19,100 people in July 2025, up 3.5 percent from the 2020 base. That is about 36 residents per square mile. Nearly three in four households own their homes, at 72.5 percent, and the Census five-year survey puts the typical owner-occupied house at $76,700. Median household income is $46,651. The county issued only 21 building permits in 2025, a small number for a county of this size.

  • The northern third of the county drains to the Altamaha River, and the southern two-thirds drains toward the Little Satilla.
  • The Edwin I. Hatch nuclear plant on U.S. 1 north of Baxley is the area's largest employer.
  • Appling County School District runs four elementary schools plus one middle and one high school.
  • Neighbors are Toombs, Tattnall, Wayne, Pierce, Jeff Davis and Bacon counties.

The county and the cities of Baxley, Graham and Surrency prepare a joint comprehensive plan, which is worth a glance if you own land on the edge of town.

How is an Appling County house valued each year?

Assessors fix a value on New Year's Day, then tax 40 percent of it. The state revenue department spells out the bill as assessed value, less any exemption, multiplied by the millage rate, where a mill is a tenth of a cent on each assessed dollar.

Appling's assessor page explains the return rules. Returns are accepted from the first of the year through April 1, but a fresh one is needed only when something changed on the parcel, such as a new building or an added acre. A skipped return that was required costs the owner a penalty of 10 percent of the unreported value, plus interest. Business equipment and other personal property gets a return every year, due April 1.

Notices arrive in May. They list the value and carry an estimated bill using the previous year's rates, but the county tells owners this estimate is not a bill. The commissioners and school board have not yet adopted budgets when the notice goes out, and millage usually gets set around September. The commissioners held their FY 2027 budget hearing on October 1, 2026, and scheduled adoption at their October 8 meeting.

What due date should I expect on an Appling bill?

The state default is a December 20 deadline with 60 days from billing to pay, but the due date on the bill itself governs. Georgia's revenue department says most counties use December 20, and it allows exceptions.

Appling bills are addressed to whoever held title at New Year. A June sale does not change that, so a seller can open the mailbox in the fall to a statement for a house that is already sold. The contract and closing statement decide who ends up paying.

  • Pay in the tax commissioner's suite, by mail, or through the county's online portal.
  • Get any open year's payoff in writing before closing day.
  • Owners of mobile homes apply to the tax commissioner for a location permit within 30 days of setting the home, then renew each year before April 2.

Call (912) 367-8105 for the current bill date and any late charges.

What is the route for disputing an Appling value?

Write the appeal and deliver it to Suite 101 within 45 days counted from the date printed on your notice. Appling's assessors state that appeals must arrive by the deadline on the notice, and that nothing is accepted once the period ends.

Allowed grounds are taxability, value and uniformity. Objecting to the tax rate itself does not qualify. On the state's PT-311A form you choose a route when you file. The assessors review the appeal first, and if they leave the value alone, the file is forwarded to a Board of Equalization, a citizen panel appointed by the grand jury. You can pick arbitration instead, and a hearing officer is open only to non-homestead real property worth more than $500,000.

After a loss, a written notice for Superior Court must reach the assessors within 30 days after the decision is mailed or handed over. Before the court hears the case, state law requires payment of tax matching the last year in which tax was found due. Georgia's revenue department has no power to overrule a local board on one parcel.

Can I claim a homestead exemption in Appling County?

Yes, for an owner who lives in the house as a legal residence. In Appling the application goes to the Tax Assessors' office, which differs from counties where the tax commissioner takes it.

File in the year the home becomes your primary residence, or any time up to April 1 of the following year. After approval it renews itself unless you want a different kind. Appling has raised its local amounts above the state minimum, and the county tax page lists the standard exemption (S1) and a preferential assessment category. Ask the assessors on (912) 367-8108 for the current dollar amounts.

The exemption stays with the owner, not the house. A buyer who moves in files in their own name, so the seller's savings end at closing and the buyer should expect a first bill without one. The county commissioners also keep a posting about a school district ad valorem exemption on their meetings page.

What if tax is unpaid when I list an Appling County house?

Plan to settle it from what the sale brings in. The debt stays attached to the parcel, and a recorded county lien must be paid off before title passes cleanly. State guidance places tax liens in the clerk's records.

Georgia puts each year's bill on the New Year's Day owner and gives no refund for part of a year. The purchase contract is where seller and buyer split the year, and the closing attorney sends the county its share. For an inherited house, the Probate Court on South Main Street handles the estate.

  • Collect a payoff statement for every open year from Suite 102.
  • Check the clerk's records for any lien on the parcel.
  • Keep your assessment notice with the closing file.
  • Confirm the settlement statement lists the tax line before you sign.

More questions about Appling County, GA Property Tax Guide

Can I pay my Appling County tax bill online?

Yes. The tax commissioner's office points owners to a county online payment portal, and it also takes payments in person at Suite 102, 69 Tippins Street in Baxley, and by mail. The office phone is (912) 367-8105.

What fraction of market value does Appling County tax?

Forty percent of the January 1 fair market value. Exemptions subtract from that assessed figure, and the millage rate then applies to what remains. One mill is $1 for every $1,000 of assessed value.

Is there any way to appeal after the notice period ends?

No. Appling's assessors say an appeal cannot be filed after the 45 days run out. The following year's notice brings the next chance, so note the deadline the day it arrives.

Who pays the tax in the year a house sells?

The owner at New Year is billed, but the sales contract can move the cost to the buyer for the months after closing. The closing attorney typically prorates the year and pays the county, so check that the settlement statement shows it.

Which phone number is for value questions?

Dial the Board of Tax Assessors at (912) 367-8108 for values, records, appeals and exemptions. Dial the Tax Commissioner at (912) 367-8105 for billing and payments.

What kind of place is Bacon County?

Bacon County is a rural, low-density county in southeast Georgia, and Alma is its seat. Wikipedia, citing Census Bureau area figures, gives it 286 square miles: 259 of land and 27 of water, or 9.5% water. The same entry notes the amendment that created the county was ratified by voters on November 3, 1914.

Streams define the map. Western and central Bacon County drains toward the Satilla River, and the eastern edge feeds the Little Satilla. Neighbors are Appling to the northeast, Pierce to the southeast, Ware to the south, Coffee to the west and Jeff Davis to the northwest. Alma is the lone city. Rockingham is a census-designated place, and Coffee and Sessoms are unincorporated.

QuickFacts estimates 11,070 residents for mid-2025, a hair below the 11,140 counted in 2020, at about 39 people per square mile. A listing here is usually a house on a country lot, often with a well, a septic tank and room for outbuildings.

How do home values and incomes look in Bacon County?

This is one of the least expensive housing markets in Georgia. For 2020-2024, QuickFacts shows a $101,400 median for homes their owners live in, and 68.6% of housing units are owner-occupied.

Bacon County at a glance (QuickFacts; most figures span 2020-2024)
ItemFigure
Owner-occupied homes, middle value$101,400
Gross rent per month, middle value$743
Household income, middle value$44,694
Housing units (July 2025)4,863
Building permits issued (2025)14
Residents in the same house a year earlier93.3%

Fourteen permits in all of 2025 means almost no new houses are going up, so a shopper compares your property with older stock. Add the fact that 93.3% of residents stayed in the same house for a year, and turnover is slow. Price against nearby recent closings rather than a statewide figure.

The 2020 census listed 4,807 housing units in Bacon County, of which 11.6% stood vacant, and 31.7% of occupied units were rented. The median age was 38.6. Those vacant houses are one reason your listing may sit beside several others that need work.

Which counter handles what in Alma?

The tax commissioner and the assessors work from the Bacon County Government Building, 502 West 12th Street, Suite 101, Alma, GA 31510. The tax commissioner's website posts one phone line, 912-632-5614, and office hours of 9:00 am to 5:00 pm.

  • Suite 101, tax commissioner: bills, payments, liens and mobile home permits
  • Suite 101, tax assessors: values, returns, exemptions and appeals
  • Suite 200, Clerk of Superior Court: copies of deeds

Parcel lookups run through qPublic. The commissioner's site also reminds visitors that its pages are general information and that the Official Code of Georgia controls.

When is the Bacon County bill due, and what does lateness cost?

Bills are normally due November 15 and are mailed at least two months earlier. Trust the date printed on your own bill, because the county warns it can change.

Two installments are allowed, though the unpaid portion keeps collecting charges after the deadline. Mail must be postmarked by that day; a deadline on a weekend or holiday moves to the next business day. You can also drive up to the box on the right side of the front parking lot. Card payments add a 2.75% charge from the processor, with a $2.00 floor.

  • Interest accrues monthly at prime plus three percentage points
  • Penalty: 5% of the tax, first applied 120 days after the due date, then every 120 days, topping out at 20%
  • Homesteaded parcels with a bill under $500 escape the penalty
  • Mobile homes run on their own April 1 deadline with a 10% penalty

Can a tax lien follow a Bacon County sale?

Yes, if the bill stays open. After 30 days of nonpayment the office can file a FiFa, a lien entered at the Clerk of Superior Court on the General Execution Docket. The county warns that the entry can stay on a credit file for seven years or longer, and that delinquent notices go out only at intervals, so call for the current amount before you pay.

State law puts the lien in the name of the January 1 owner. To switch it to the buyer, bring the signed closing statement to Suite 101 within 90 days after the due date. A bill that reaches you after you sold belongs in the buyer's hands.

  1. Request a written balance from Suite 101.
  2. Direct the title company to pay it out of your proceeds.
  3. File away your settlement statement.

How do I contest a Bacon County value?

The clock is 45 days and starts on the date printed on the assessment notice. Send the assessors a written dispute on the uniform state form, and name your ground: taxability, value, uniformity or a refused exemption.

The same filing names the track you choose. On the Board of Equalization track, the assessors may first revise the figure, which gives you 30 days to answer an amended notice; anything unresolved is heard by the board, and Superior Court sits beyond that. A hearing officer track exists for non-homestead real estate above a value threshold. Arbitration requires a certified appraisal and ends the matter.

Separately, the January 1 to April 1 return period lets you declare your own value. Real estate returns renew themselves each year, while personal property returns need filing annually.

Which breaks can lower a Bacon County bill?

Homestead is the main one. The state constitution sets a baseline, Bacon County adds local exemptions, and whichever is larger controls. You must have owned and lived in the house on January 1, and the form must reach the assessors by April 1 of your first claim year; after approval it renews itself.

  • Deferral for homeowners 62 and up whose household income is no more than $15,000
  • Qualifying farmland: assessed at 30% rather than 40%
  • Conservation Use and Forest Land Protection: valued by current use, with a 10 or 15 year covenant
  • Historic and brownfield programs: filed in the same January to April window

Call 912-632-5614 for the local amounts and what proof to bring. Claiming homestead on a second property anywhere, in or out of Georgia, is unlawful.

How should a Bacon County sale be ordered when tax is owed?

Begin with the number. Learn the balance for each open year, whether a FiFa exists, and, if the house is a mobile home, whether the April 1 permit tax is paid. Then choose between paying before you list and paying at the closing table.

Inherited houses, rentals and vacant properties often carry several unpaid years, and a title search will surface every recorded lien. If your land sits in a conservation or forest program, ask the assessors what the covenant demands of a new owner before you list, since a buyer will ask.

More questions about Bacon County, GA Property Tax Guide

What share of market value is taxed in Bacon County?

Forty percent of fair market value is the assessed value, and exemptions come off that figure before the millage rate is applied. The county commissioners and the school board set the rate each year.

How can I pay a Bacon County bill?

Pay at Suite 101 of the Government Building in Alma, by mail with a postmark on or before the deadline, in the drop box, or online with a card. Questions go to 912-632-5614.

Does selling split the bill between buyer and seller?

Your closing statement does that, not the county. The tax commissioner asks you to bring the signed statement to Suite 101 within 90 days after the due date if you want a lien recorded against the buyer.

Is there a refund if I sell in March?

No. Georgia's Department of Revenue says the owner on January 1 is responsible for the entire year, and it allows no refund for a part-year owner.

Who sends the notice of my home's value?

The Board of Tax Assessors in the same building. Call 912-632-5614, and mind the 45-day clock that starts on the date printed on the notice.

Baldwin County by the numbers

Why does Baldwin County stand apart in central Georgia?

Baldwin County holds Milledgeville, a college town that was once Georgia's capital. Land the Creek ceded in the 1802 Treaty of Fort Wilkinson went into the county, which the General Assembly created on May 11, 1803; it is named for Abraham Baldwin, a Constitution signer and founder of the University of Georgia. Milledgeville served as capital from 1804 to 1868, per Wikipedia.

Georgia College and State University and Georgia Military College, which occupies the Old Capitol building, give the city its college-town character. A December 1807 act later split Morgan, Jones, Putnam and Jasper counties off the Baldwin of that era. The old Governor's Mansion and the historic district add to a housing stock that ranges widely in age. Central State Hospital, which the legislature provided for in 1837, is another long-standing institution.

The county measures 267 square miles and straddles the fall line. Terrain is hillier in the north, in the Piedmont, and flatter toward the south, at the top edge of the coastal plain. Land south of Lake Sinclair drains to the Lower Oconee River. Putnam, Hancock, Washington, Wilkinson and Jones counties adjoin it. Hardwick, a census-designated place, and the unincorporated Scottsboro round out the map.

What do QuickFacts numbers show for Baldwin County housing?

Rental housing plays a large part in Baldwin County. QuickFacts lists 61.1% of housing units as owner-occupied for 2020-2024 and $181,900 as the middle home value.

Baldwin County at a glance (QuickFacts; most figures span 2020-2024)
ItemFigure
Owner-occupied homes, middle value$181,900
Gross rent per month, middle value$923
Household income, middle value$54,403
Housing units (July 2025)20,797
Building permits issued (2025)95
Residents (July 2025 estimate)44,029

In the 2020 count, 19,988 housing units were on the books, with 17.4% empty and 42.1% of occupied units rented; the rental vacancy rate was 14.5%. Of 16,511 households, 31.7% were one person living alone. Population fell 4.2% from 2010 to 2020 before inching up in the estimates, and 48.8% of residents lived in rural areas. The 2020 census counted 43,799 people, 9,568 families and a median age of 38.4, with 18.4% of residents under 18 and 17.3% 65 or older. A seller might hold a lot inside Milledgeville or acreage out in the county, and the two attract different buyers. With 42.1% of occupied units rented in 2020, investors are a natural audience for a rental house you want to sell as it stands.

Who runs property tax in Baldwin County?

Find the tax commissioner in the Baldwin County Government Building, 1601 N. Columbia Street, Suite 100, Milledgeville, GA 31061. The county's tax site lists 478-445-4813 and weekday hours from 8:30 in the morning until 4:45 in the afternoon, closed on holidays.

Valuation questions belong with the tax assessors, (478) 445-5300, and parcel data lives on qPublic. The county board, five members each elected from a single district, helps set the county share of the millage rate, while the school board sets its own.

  • Tax commissioner: bills, payments, liens, closing statements
  • Tax assessors: values, returns, exemptions, appeals
  • Clerk of Superior Court: recorded deeds and liens

Which due date should Baldwin County owners believe?

Trust the bill in your hand. One county page names December 15, and another says November 15 is the general date, with bills going out no later than 60 days before it.

The bill can be split across two payments, and any unpaid remainder keeps accruing. Mailed checks must carry a postmark no later than the deadline; if that day is a Saturday, Sunday or holiday, you get the next business day. The front lot has a drop box. Cards add a processor fee of 2.57% (3% for American Express), with a $1.50 minimum.

  • Interest builds monthly at prime plus 3 points
  • A 5% penalty arrives 120 days past the deadline and recurs at 120-day intervals until the total hits 20%
  • No penalty applies to homesteaded property when the bill is under $500
  • Mobile homes: April 1 deadline, 10% penalty, and a possible citation to State Court

How do I handle an unpaid Baldwin County bill when I sell?

Ask the tax commissioner for a payoff in writing, then have the closing agent settle it out of your proceeds. The year's tax is tied to the January 1 owner, and the office says it files any lien under that owner's name unless Suite 100 receives a closing statement, within 90 days after the due date, showing the buyer took on the bill.

A bill that keeps coming to you after closing should be passed to the buyer, and the office should get a copy of the settlement statement. Leave a bill unpaid and a FiFa lien goes onto the General Execution Docket at the Clerk of Superior Court, where the county says it can sit on credit files for seven years or more.

Have the payoff dated. Interest is added monthly and delinquent bills are not mailed monthly, so last week's figure can fall short. If the house was a rental, an inheritance or sat empty, ask for the history of each year you held it.

What is the Baldwin County appeal path?

The deadline is 45 days after the date on the assessment notice. Submit a written appeal to the Board of Tax Assessors using the state's form; the permitted arguments are taxability, value, uniformity and a denied exemption.

Your filing also selects a route. On the Board of Equalization route, the assessors may amend the value first, which opens a 30-day window to challenge the amended notice; otherwise a hearing is scheduled, and Superior Court comes after. A hearing officer, who must be a certified appraiser, is open only for non-homestead real property valued at $1,000,000 or more, according to the county's tax site. Arbitration requires a certified appraisal and cannot be appealed further.

State revenue officials cannot override the assessors, a board, a hearing officer, an arbitrator or a court on one parcel's value. Mobile home owners have 45 days from the mailing of their bill or April 1, whichever falls later.

Which Baldwin County exemptions are worth checking?

Baldwin County layers local homestead exemptions over the state's, and the larger amount governs. Applications go to the assessors, who must have them by April 1 of your first claim year; approved ones renew automatically.

  • You must own the house and live in it on January 1 of that first year
  • A second homestead claim, in Georgia or elsewhere, is not allowed
  • Owners aged 62 or more with household income up to $15,000 can defer the tax
  • Qualifying farmland is assessed at 30% instead of 40%; current-use programs ask for a 10 or 15 year covenant

Phone (478) 445-5300 for current amounts, and carry proof of age, income or service if your exemption turns on it.

More questions about Baldwin County, GA Property Tax Guide

Who do I call about my Baldwin County tax bill?

Dial 478-445-4813 for the tax commissioner, whose office is at 1601 N. Columbia Street, Suite 100, Milledgeville.

Can I pay online in Baldwin County?

Yes. An online payment page exists, with a processor fee on cards. The counter, the mail and the drop box are the other options.

Does a sale wipe out the bill for that year?

No. The January 1 owner stays on the record unless your closing statement reaches the office within 90 days after the due date.

What fraction of value is taxed in Baldwin County?

Assessed value is set at 40% of fair market value, or 30% for qualifying agricultural land, and exemptions are subtracted before the millage rate is applied.

What is the deadline to contest a Baldwin County value?

Forty-five days, counted from the notice date. A mobile home gets 45 days from the mailing of its bill or April 1, whichever is later.

Which towns sit inside Banks County, and how did it begin?

Banks County lies in Georgia's northeast corner and Homer is its seat. The General Assembly passed the founding act on December 11, 1858, and the county took effect on February 1, 1859, cut from Franklin and Habersham counties (Wikipedia).

Wikipedia, using Census Bureau area data, gives the county 234 square miles, with 232 of them land. All of it falls within the Broad River sub-basin of the Savannah River basin, and a slice of the Chattahoochee National Forest reaches in. Habersham, Stephens, Franklin, Madison, Jackson and Hall counties touch the border.

Cities listed are Baldwin, Commerce, Gillsville and Lula; towns are Alto, Homer and Maysville. Several of these straddle a line with Habersham, Jackson or Hall. Hollingsworth and Narrows are unincorporated. Because a mailing address can name a town that sits partly in a neighboring county, check the parcel record to learn which tax commissioner bills you.

Homer's Old Banks County Courthouse is on the National Register of Historic Places, and a newer courthouse went up beside it in 1983. Atlanta Dragway operates near Banks Crossing. Banks County School District, headquartered in Homer, runs four schools for roughly 2,788 students, and The Banks County News serves as the legal organ.

How fast is Banks County growing, and what do homes cost?

Growth has been brisk lately. The 2020 census counted 18,035 residents, and QuickFacts estimates 21,273 for mid-2025, up 17.6% from its adjusted 2020 base. For 2020-2024 the middle household income is $77,063 and the middle owner-occupied home is valued at $278,100.

Banks County at a glance (QuickFacts; most figures span 2020-2024)
ItemFigure

A 32.7-minute commute is the second longest among the four counties in the QuickFacts comparison, behind Barrow. In the 2020 count, 95.6% of residents lived in rural areas, with 7,211 housing units and 7.8% of them vacant. That count also showed 6,652 households, with children under 18 in 33.9% of them, a median age of 40.6, and 77.8% of occupied units owned by their residents.

The long view is steeper than the recent one. Banks County had 6,497 people in 1960, 14,422 in 2000 and 18,395 in 2010, then slipped to 18,035 in 2020 before the newer estimate jumped. A county that nearly tripled between 1960 and 2010 has plenty of houses of very different ages, from farmhouses to recent subdivisions, and buyers compare them closely.

Where do Banks County property tax questions go?

The tax commissioner bills and collects for the county, the state, the school board and community improvement districts. Property taxes are paid at Suite 7 of the Courthouse Annex, 150 Hudson Ridge, Homer, GA 30547. The county's payment page says the Annex keeps weekday hours of 8 am to 5 pm.

The phone for tax bills is 706-677-6204. For valuation, appeals, or news that a property was sold or a business closed after January 1, call the Board of Assessors at 706-677-6223. The commissioner honors a U.S. Postal Service postmark dated by midnight of the deadline; a postage-meter date does not count as proof.

  • Suite 7: property taxes in person
  • Tax commissioner phone: 706-677-6204
  • Board of Assessors phone: 706-677-6223

What does a Banks County assessment notice tell me?

Every owner of taxable real property gets an annual notice. It lists the fair market value fixed by the Board of Tax Assessors and the assessed value, which state law sets at 40%.

The assessors study sales in groups, by neighborhood, property type and use, and adjust whole groups when market evidence says values have drifted. A changed value shows on the notice. Disagreeing owners have 45 days from the notice date to appeal, on grounds of taxability, value or non-uniform assessment.

Bills usually arrive in September. If your parcel was under appeal then, the bill used a temporary value: the smaller of last year's value or 85% of this year's original notice value. It remained due on the printed date. After the appeal ends, the commissioner decides whether a supplemental bill or a credit follows.

How should I handle Banks County tax during a sale?

The tax commissioner states that it does not prorate tax between a buyer and a seller. Liability is settled at closing, usually with the purchaser assuming it, and your closing paperwork shows who pays. The tax attaches to the property, so whoever holds title should confirm it is paid.

A business that closed, or a property that sold, after January 1 still owes tax for the full year, and the Board of Assessors should be told. If a mortgage company pays your tax, the office would like you to forward them a copy of the bill.

  • A missing bill is not an excuse; copies are online or at the office
  • Partial payments are accepted until the bill is paid, by arrangement at 706-677-6204
  • Write the parcel ID on a check or money order

What if a Banks County appeal is still open on the due date?

Pay at least the appealed amount by the due date, the county's FAQ says, or a 1% penalty applies. Payment cannot be put off, and the assessors cannot extend the deadline. Interest of 1% per month, capped at $150, builds on the rest, and paying the full bill by the due date avoids it.

When you plan to sell during an appeal, tell your closing agent. The final figure may change, a supplemental bill or credit may follow, and you should agree in writing who keeps any refund.

How do Banks County exemptions get approved?

Nothing here is automatic; each exemption needs its own application. The name on the deed must match the applicant, who must own, occupy and claim the home as a legal residence on January 1. The county asks for proof of residency and citizenship or legal authorization, plus current registration or receipts for vehicles owned in Banks County.

A married couple counts as one applicant and gets one exemption. Once granted it renews, and a refinance does not require filing again. Changes of name or ownership through marriage, death or divorce mean reapplying with a recorded deed, marriage certificate or divorce decree. Faxed or emailed applications are rejected; an original must arrive, or carry a non-metered postmark, by the April 1 deadline for a first-year claim.

Forms and instructions are on the county's Tax Assessors page. Look there for current local amounts before you list.

What is the first move for a Banks County seller with tax due?

Call 706-677-6204 and ask what is owed on the parcel for the current and any earlier years. If part of the balance is under appeal, say so in the same call, since the temporary-value bill rules apply. Then give your closing agent the amount and the Suite 7 address, 150 Hudson Ridge, Homer.

If an exemption is on the property and you are moving, tell the tax commissioner when you no longer qualify. The county's FAQ says the office must be notified if the applicant no longer meets the requirements, and a change of ownership means the new owner must apply on their own.

More questions about Banks County, GA Property Tax Guide

Where do I pay a Banks County property tax bill?

Go to Suite 7 of the Courthouse Annex at 150 Hudson Ridge, Homer, GA 30547, open weekdays from 8 am to 5 pm. Mailing a payment or using the online payment link also works.

Will the Banks County tax commissioner divide the bill between me and the buyer?

No. The office says it stays out of the buyer and seller proration. Your closing documents decide who pays.

Can I submit a faxed homestead form in Banks County?

No. The county's FAQ says an original must be received or postmarked by the deadline, and faxed or emailed copies are not accepted.

May I pay a Banks County bill in pieces?

Yes. Partial payments are accepted until the bill is satisfied, and the county asks you to call 706-677-6204 to set it up. Interest keeps accruing on what remains.

What if no bill ever came?

The responsibility to pay by the due date still stands. A copy is on the county website or available from the tax commissioner.

Barrow County by the numbers

What towns and cities make up Barrow County?

Barrow County lies in east central Georgia on the edge of the Atlanta metro area, and Winder is its seat. Voters approved the amendment that created it on November 3, 1914, using pieces of Gwinnett, Jackson and Walton counties; it became the state's 149th county of what are now 159 (Wikipedia).

It is a small county by area, 163 square miles with 160 of them land, and all of it drains into the Upper Oconee River sub-basin of the Altamaha River basin. Gwinnett lies to the west, Walton to the south, Oconee to the southeast, Jackson to the east and Hall to the north; Clarke County meets it at a single point.

  • Cities: Auburn, Statham and Winder
  • Towns: Bethlehem, Braselton (mostly Jackson County, partly Gwinnett and Hall) and Carl
  • Census-designated place: Russell
  • Unincorporated: Barrow Heights, Mulberry and Whistleville

Since Braselton spans several counties, a Braselton owner should read the parcel record to see which county's tax commissioner sends the bill.

How quickly has Barrow County added people and houses?

Very quickly. The census counted 21,354 residents in 1980, 46,144 in 2000, 69,367 in 2010 and 83,505 in 2020, and QuickFacts estimates 99,773 for mid-2025. The 2020 count showed 30,019 housing units and 28,727 households, 38.8% of them with children, and a median age of 36.4.

Compare the 1,584 permits with the 14 in Bacon County and the picture is clear: Barrow County is still building. QuickFacts lists 518.5 people per square mile, against 39.2 in Bacon County, and 78.5% of housing units are owner-occupied. In the 2020 count, 67.0% of residents lived in urban areas, 77.4% of occupied units were owned, and the homeowner vacancy rate was 1.5%. A seller in a newer subdivision near Winder or Auburn will be listed beside many similar houses, so price and condition carry extra weight.

Which school cluster serves a Barrow County address?

Barrow County Schools is the sole district, and its schools group into two clusters named for Winder-Barrow High School and Apalachee High School. A buyer's school assignment depends on the cluster serving the address.

  • Winder-Barrow: Winder-Barrow High, Richard B. Russell Middle, Bear Creek Middle, and Holsenbeck, Bramlett, Statham, County Line and Winder elementary schools
  • Apalachee: Apalachee High, Westside Middle, Haymon-Morris Middle, and Auburn, Kennedy, Bethlehem and Yargo elementary schools
  • Also listed: Barrow Arts and Sciences Academy

This list comes from Wikipedia, so confirm attendance zones with the district before naming a school in a listing.

Who sends the bill and who sets the value in Barrow County?

The tax commissioner works from 30 N. Broad Street, Winder, GA 30680. The Barrow County Tax Portal gives (770) 307-3106 and weekday hours of 8:00 to 4:30. Card payments carry a 2.5% service fee, minimum $1.50. The portal also says vehicle transactions require a Georgia driver's license or ID card with a Barrow County address.

Values are the Tax Assessors Office's job, at the same street address, and the county invites calls between 8 and 5 on weekdays. Notices can be printed from qPublic. The commissioner picks the due date and mails the bill but has no say over your value.

When do Barrow County notices and bills arrive?

The county's 2024 release said real property and personal property notices (aircraft, boats, business equipment) went out May 1, while final tax bills would wait until September and fall due in November. Treat that as the normal rhythm, and rely on the date on your own bill.

A notice is not a bill. It estimates tax from the assessed value. If you disagree, you have 45 days to appeal, either online through qPublic, by mail, or in person at the Tax Assessors Office.

  • Permitted grounds: taxability, value, uniformity or a denied exemption
  • Tracks: Board of Equalization, hearing officer or arbitrator
  • State revenue officials cannot override a board, hearing officer, arbitrator or court on one parcel

What can I look up online before listing a Barrow County house?

Two sites cover most of it. The tax portal lets you search information on any property in the county, pay property tax and renew car tags online. The assessors' qPublic pages let you print the current and prior year assessment notices from the assessment section, which helps when a buyer's agent asks what the value was last year.

Pay attention to the returned-check rule on the tax portal: if a bank dishonors your check, a service fee is assessed under state law, and the county uses Envision Payment Solutions for recovery, reachable at 1-877-290-5460. For a closing, a certified payment avoids that problem.

The county's own notice adds that the assessors will answer questions about an assessment notice or the appeal process by phone on weekdays, so a seller who expects a challenge can start that conversation before the 45 days run out.

Can a city also bill me inside Barrow County?

Possibly. A parcel inside a city may be taxed by the city as well as the county, so ask the city clerk whether a separate bill exists. With three cities and three towns here, never assume a county payoff covers any municipal balance.

Georgia's revenue department says the owner on January 1 answers for the whole year's tax even if the house sells on January 2, and no refund is allowed for part of a year. The title company should request a current payoff from each billing office and settle both at closing.

If an earlier year is unpaid, the tax commissioner's office can say whether a lien was recorded.

What becomes of surplus money after a Barrow County tax sale?

Barrow County's real property page says it works with Weissman Excess Funds Management on surplus from tax sales. The firm publishes open records on the funds it handles, typically refreshed on the 1st and 15th of each month, and you request information by email.

The page states plainly that Barrow County does not release excess funds to third parties. Someone who lost property to a tax sale should contact the Tax Commissioner's Office or the firm directly about a claim, rather than pay a stranger to chase it.

Where do Barrow County homestead applications go?

Georgia gives a standard homestead exemption to owners who live in the home as their primary residence, and many counties add richer local ones. The state says applications go to the county tax commissioner or the assessors, depending on the county.

Phone (770) 307-3106 to learn which Barrow County office takes yours, and bring proof of residency. After the exemption is subtracted from assessed value, the millage rate is applied to what remains.

More questions about Barrow County, GA Property Tax Guide

Where is the Barrow County tax commissioner?

At 30 N. Broad Street in Winder, GA 30680. Call (770) 307-3106 on weekdays between 8:00 and 4:30.

Does a Barrow County assessment notice require payment?

No, it is an estimate of tax based on assessed value, not a bill. Final bills follow later, in September according to the county's 2024 announcement.

What is the way to appeal a Barrow County value?

Act within 45 days of the notice. Appeals may be filed online through qPublic, by mail, or at the Tax Assessors Office at 30 N. Broad Street.

Are tax sale surplus funds paid out to third parties in Barrow County?

No. The county states that it does not release excess funds to third parties, and claims run through its Tax Commissioner's Office and excess funds partner.

Who pays if I sell a Barrow County house mid-year?

The January 1 owner is liable for the full year under Georgia law, with no part-year refund. Divide the bill with the buyer in your closing paperwork.

Bartow County by the numbers

Who sends the tax bill in Bartow County, Georgia?

The Bartow County Tax Commissioner mails and collects the bill, while a separate Board of Tax Assessors puts the value on your land and house. Payments, mobile home accounts and tax sale overage claims all go to the commissioner's suite inside the Frank Moore Administration and Judicial Building, 135 W. Cherokee Avenue, Suite 217A, Cartersville. The property tax line is (770) 387-5111, and the counter is open Monday through Friday, eight in the morning until five, holidays excepted.

Bartow runs on a sole commissioner form of government. One elected commissioner adopts the budget and sets the millage in a public meeting held at that same building, and the county's own minutes show the 2026 rates were approved on August 5. Cartersville is the county seat. Adairsville, Euharlee, Kingston and Taylorsville hold their own charters, and Cassville, Rydal and Allatoona are unincorporated communities that still pay through the county office.

  • Tax Commissioner: statements, payments, duplicate bills, excess funds forms.
  • Board of Tax Assessors: values, returns and the notices that carry appeal rights.
  • County Commissioner: adopts the rates and the budget each summer.

What should a Bartow County homeowner weigh before selling?

Bartow sits in the northwest of Georgia, and the Cartersville end of it now behaves like an Atlanta exurb, reached by I-75 more than 40 miles from downtown. The county was carved from Cherokee land in 1832 as Cass County and took the Bartow name in 1861. The Great Locomotive Chase of 1862 passed through, and the Etowah Indian Mounds, the Booth Western Art Museum and Tellus Science Museum still draw visitors today.

Roughly 459 square miles of land stretch from the Etowah River basin to Lake Allatoona and Red Top Mountain State Park on the southeast edge. Drivers use US 41, US 411 and state routes 20, 61, 113, 140 and 293. A house in Cartersville falls under Cartersville City Schools, while most other addresses belong to the Bartow County School District, so confirm the district before you describe a listing to a buyer.

The county's population moved from 100,157 in 2010 to 108,901 in 2020, and the Census Bureau estimate for mid-2025 is 120,800. County leaders credit a large industrial base, a battery plant and data center development for the tax digest growth that has let the millage keep falling.

The Census Bureau lists 50,010 housing units in 2025, with 72.8 percent of households owning, a median owner-occupied value of $289,000, median rent of $1,268 a month and median household income of $82,243. Workers travel 29.4 minutes on average to a job.

When do Bartow County property taxes come due?

Statements for real estate leave the office around September 15, and the due date is November 15. For 2026 that date was November 15, 2026. Mobile homes follow their own cycle with an April 1 due date.

Whoever owned the parcel on January 1 is the billed party. If you closed on a purchase after that date, phone the tax office and ask for a duplicate in your name, because the first statement went to the previous owner. The county adds that a bill that never arrives does not move the deadline.

  • Online payment sits behind a link on the Tax Commissioner page, and the same page lists qpublic for parcel lookups.
  • Debit and credit cards, whether paid online, at the counter or by phone, add a 2.5 percent convenience charge.
  • A check by mail is made out to the Bartow County Tax Commissioner at the Cherokee Avenue address.

Georgia gives every taxpayer 60 days from the postmark on the bill before interest starts, and delinquent balances can also draw penalties. Ask the office for the figure that applies to your account.

What are Bartow County's 2026 millage rates?

The 2026 rate is 7.11 mills inside city limits and 6.76 mills in the unincorporated county. Last year's figures were 7.40 and 6.87. According to the August minutes, the commissioner chose the rollback rate and noted that rates have trended down since 2013.

A mill is a dollar of tax on each $1,000 of assessed value, and assessed value is set at 40 percent of what the board calls fair market value. The school board levies its own rate on top, so your statement will show more than the county figure alone. Rather than estimate, ask the tax office for the combined millage tied to your parcel and district.

How do I claim the homestead exemption in Bartow County?

File with the county before April 1, and only for the home where you live. The billing page is blunt that rentals, multi-family buildings and commercial or industrial property are excluded.

The commissioner's August 2026 minutes put the standard exemption at $15,000 of value and say the county is working with the legislature on a move to $30,000 in a future year. Because that is a goal and not a promise, call the office to learn the amount on your current bill. Moving to another Bartow house means filing again for the new address.

How can I challenge a Bartow County property value?

Mail a written appeal to the Board of Tax Assessors with a postmark no later than 45 days after the notice date. Georgia sets that window for every county, and it covers disputes about fair market value.

Before any notice arrives, owners may file a return between January 1 and April 1 stating the value they believe is right. Money paid on tax that was wrongly charged can be claimed back within three years of payment, and refunds from a winning appeal are issued automatically. Gather sale prices of nearby houses and dated photos of damage before you write the appeal.

How does a sale interact with the Bartow County tax bill?

The unpaid tax rides with the property, so closing is the moment to settle it. Because the county names the January 1 owner, a seller who held title on that day normally gets the statement even if the deed changes hands in October. Ask whoever handles your closing to show how the year's bill is split and who sends the payment.

When back taxes pile up and the county sells the parcel for more than is owed, the excess is held for the people with a claim. The commissioner's page links an excess funds form for that situation. Selling before a levy usually costs less than waiting, so request a written payoff from the office and compare it with any offer you receive.

More questions about Bartow County, GA Property Tax Guide

When were 2026 property taxes due in Bartow County?

November 15, 2026, with statements mailed around September 15. Mobile home bills are due April 1.

What is the last day to apply for homestead in Bartow County?

April 1. The exemption only covers the home you live in as a primary residence.

How many days do I get to appeal a Bartow assessment?

45 days from the date the notice was mailed, with the written appeal postmarked inside that window and sent to the Board of Tax Assessors.

Will Bartow County send my bill to the lender?

No, statements go to whoever held title on January 1, so ask your lender whether it pays from escrow. A buyer who closed after January 1 can ask the office at (770) 387-5111 for a duplicate statement.

Does Bartow County charge a fee to pay by card?

Yes, 2.5 percent on debit and credit payments, whether made online, in person or by phone. A check by mail carries no such fee.

Which Ben Hill County offices handle property tax?

Two offices share the work in Ben Hill County. The Tax Commissioner at 324 East Pine Street in Fitzgerald sends bills and takes payments, and the Board of Tax Assessors decides what the property is worth. Call the commissioner at (229) 426-5144 Monday through Friday, with the counter staffed until half past four, and reach the assessors at (229) 426-5147.

Questions about a payment, a lien or a mailing address belong with the commissioner. Questions about value, a homestead file or an exemption belong with the assessors. The county's assessor page also tells owners that appraisers inspect properties on an ongoing basis, that every parcel with a building permit is visited, and that mobile homes are checked for a current decal.

  • Tax Commissioner: statements, receipts, liens, online payments.
  • Board of Tax Assessors: value, returns, exemptions, notices of assessment.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: copies of your warranty deed, kept in the deed room at the courthouse.

What is Fitzgerald and Ben Hill County like for a home seller?

Ben Hill is a small south Georgia county, and Fitzgerald is its only city as well as its seat. The legislature created it in 1906 out of Irwin and Wilcox land, and of its 254 square miles only about four are water. Neighbors are Wilcox, Telfair, Coffee, Irwin and Turner. The courthouse and the old county jail are both on the National Register of Historic Places.

Fitzgerald High School is the county's high school, and the Ben Hill County School District also runs a preschool, a primary school, an elementary school and a middle school. Headcount slipped from 17,194 at the 2020 census to a 2025 estimate of 17,099. Census figures list a middle home value of $112,700 against a middle household income of $41,758, which frames how much a tax bill matters to an owner here.

The Census Bureau lists 8,166 housing units in 2025 and a 63.3 percent owner rate. Median gross rent is $688 a month, 22.2 percent of residents are in poverty and the average commute is only 16.8 minutes.

When does the Ben Hill County bill come due, and what does lateness cost?

Per the tax office FAQ, December 1 is the usual date for land, houses and business personal property. Georgia's default is December 20 and counties may move it, so trust the day printed on your own statement. One mobile home answer on the same FAQ gives April 1 and another gives May 1, so ask the office which date applies to your mobile home account.

Late accounts accrue interest of 1% a month. A one-time 10% penalty applies once 90 days pass, except that a homesteaded parcel owing under $500 escapes that penalty. A balance older than 90 days can also become a FiFa lien in the Clerk of Superior Court's records, where credit bureaus may see it, and the commissioner is then free to levy on the parcel.

Statements go to the owner, not the lender. With an escrow account, pass the bill along or check that the servicer is paying it.

How can I pay my Ben Hill County property tax?

Cash and checks at the counter cost nothing extra, and a mailed check works as well. Online payment through the county's GovtWindow portal is available through the portal, with PayPal and cards offered only on the website. Each online method adds a convenience charge that appears before you confirm, so you can stop and pay by check instead.

  • In person: 324 East Pine Street, Fitzgerald, Georgia 31750.
  • By phone for questions: (229) 426-5144.
  • Portal help line: (877) 575-7233.
Late-payment and payment-method rules from the Ben Hill Tax Commissioner FAQ
RuleWhat the office says

Penalty10% if unpaid 90 days past the deadline

Who qualifies for homestead in Ben Hill County?

Owning and living in the house on January 1 is the test, and the application has to land at the assessors' office ahead of April 1. A filing carries forward each year while you stay put. Move, and you reapply for the new address, while a late filing simply pushes the benefit to the next tax year.

The tax office FAQ notes that homeowners who reach age 62 can apply for an additional exemption. Business inventory can qualify for a freeport exemption where local voters have approved one. For the dollar amount on your own bill, call the assessors, since local legislation can increase the base amounts.

How are values set and challenged in Ben Hill County?

Each winter and early spring, up to the first of April, an owner may file a return naming a value. If the board disagrees it mails a notice with its figure. Taxable value is 40% of market value, and every mill raises one dollar for each $1,000 of that taxable value.

The clock for an appeal is 45 days from the notice date, and the appeal goes to the county Board of Equalization or to an arbitrator. Unhappy with that result, you can continue in superior court by delivering written notice to the assessors. Refund requests for tax charged in error have a three-year limit, counted from payment.

What should a Ben Hill County seller sort out on taxes before closing?

Learn the balance and the billed owner before you sign. Because the January 1 owner is on the statement, it can carry your name even when the buyer takes the deed later in the year. Ask the commissioner for a printed balance, and ask whoever runs the closing how that year is shared with the buyer.

A recorded lien must be cleared before clean title can pass. Most sellers settle it out of the sale money, and the commissioner's payoff number is the amount to wire. Needed repairs do not stop a sale while taxes are owed.

What should a mobile home owner in Ben Hill County do about tax?

Mobile and modular homes count as personal property in Georgia, so the owner files a return and obtains a location permit each year. The county FAQ states that the current year's mobile home tax must be paid in full before the permit is issued, and it lists April 1 as the due date in that answer. Another line of the same FAQ mentions May 1, which is why a call to the commissioner is worth making.

The assessors also check mobile homes for a current decal during their inspections. Selling one means the next owner inherits the paperwork trail, so settle the year's tax and the permit before you hand over the home. Keep the paid receipt, since the permit cannot be issued until the tax is paid.

The assessor page also carries a 2026 meeting calendar for the Board of Assessors, a 2026 deadlines sheet and a returned mail listing. Owners who moved and never updated an address should check that list so notices reach them.

When is real estate tax due in Ben Hill County?

Where do Berrien County property owners deal with tax?

The Tax Commissioner is in Suite 105 on the ground floor of the Administration Building, 201 N. Davis Street, Nashville, Georgia 31639. Billing and payment questions go to (229) 686-7461, and the counter takes visitors on weekdays from eight until five. The commissioner bills and collects real property, personal property, mobile home, motor vehicle and timber tax.

Valuation is a different office. Berrien's Board of Tax Assessors sets values and takes homestead applications, and the Tax Commissioner's staff can point you to the assessors if you are unsure where to go.

  • Tax Commissioner: bills, receipts, payment help, liens.
  • Tax Assessor: values, returns, homestead and other exemptions.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: warranty deed copies at the courthouse deed room.

What should a Berrien County seller know about the county itself?

Berrien lies in south central Georgia, and a legislative act of February 25, 1856 carved it out of Coffee, Irwin and Lowndes. It spans 458 square miles, most of it rural, with the western side draining toward the Withlacoochee River and the eastern side toward the Alapaha. Irwin, Coffee, Atkinson, Lanier, Lowndes, Cook and Tift counties touch its borders. One school system, the Berrien County School District, covers every address.

The county lost an unusually high share of its young men in World War I, and a copper Doughboy memorial by E. M. Viquesney stands on the Nashville courthouse grounds. Headcount has swung: 19,286 in 2010, then 18,160, then an estimated 18,932 for 2025. Nearly three quarters of residents counted in 2020 lived outside urban areas, so most owners hold rural parcels rather than town lots.

The Census Bureau lists 8,328 housing units in 2025 and a 71.0 percent owner rate. Median household income is $52,876, and 18.0 percent of residents live in poverty.

When must Berrien County property tax be paid?

According to the tax office, houses, land and business equipment have been billed for a November 15 deadline each year since 2018. Mobile and manufactured homes keep an April 1 deadline, and vehicles follow the owner's birthday.

The same FAQ spells out lateness. A month of delay adds 1% interest, and a flat 10% penalty lands if the bill is still open three months after the deadline. Unpaid tax can turn into a FiFa lien at the Clerk of Superior Court, which the FAQ says is possible once a bill is 30 days overdue, and ultimately the commissioner may levy on the parcel.

Berrien's tax site runs on the GovtWindow platform, which lets owners search a parcel and pay online, and its help desk number is (877) 575-7233. Mobile and modular homes count as personal property in Georgia, so the owner files a return and gets a location permit, and the permit is issued only after that year's mobile home tax is paid in full. Timber tax is also billed by the commissioner, which matters for anyone selling acreage.

Berrien County payment calendar and late charges, per the Tax Commissioner FAQ

How does Berrien County calculate a tax bill?

The state taxes 40% of market value, and Berrien's county commissioners and school board each choose a millage every year. The tax office lays out the order of operations: take assessed value, subtract exemptions to reach net taxable value, then multiply by the mills. A mill raises one dollar on each $1,000 of that net figure.

Ask the commissioner for the millage on your parcel instead of guessing at it. Statements go to the owner. A lender that escrows for you needs a copy, so check that the servicer has the Berrien bill.

  • Returns: owners can name their own value any time in the first three months of the year.
  • Notice: the assessors send one when their value differs from the return.
  • Bill: the commissioner applies the adopted mills to net taxable value.

How is homestead claimed in Berrien County?

Both owning and occupying the house on New Year's Day are required. The application goes to the tax assessor's office and must be received before April 1. Filing is allowed year round, though a late application starts with the next tax year.

Approval carries over year to year at the same address. A move to another Berrien house means filing anew. Homeowners at 62 may apply for an added exemption, and business personal property can qualify for freeport relief. The dollar figures change with legislation, so the assessors are the source for current amounts.

What are my options if I dispute a Berrien County value?

The deadline is 45 days counted from the notice date. Take the appeal to the county Board of Equalization or an arbitrator, and if you remain dissatisfied, tell the Board of Tax Assessors in writing that you are continuing to superior court.

State guidance says a fair market value appeal sent by mail needs a postmark no later than day 45. Tax collected in error or illegally can be recovered when a written claim is made inside three years of payment.

What tax steps come before selling a Berrien County house?

Request the balance in writing from the commissioner before taking an offer, and confirm who is billed. The owner on January 1 gets the statement, so yours may still arrive after a fall closing. Whoever handles the closing can show how that year's tax is divided.

A FiFa on file is public and must be satisfied before the buyer gets a clean title. Farmhouses with old taxes, inherited deeds or deferred repairs can still sell as is, since the payoff is taken from the sale money. A cash buyer will ask for the same payoff number you hold. If the house is a rural parcel, also ask whether any timber tax or a mobile home account is attached to the same owner, since the commissioner bills those too, and settle each one before the deed is signed.

What do Census numbers say about Berrien County households?

The Census Bureau counts 7,045 households with an average of 2.58 people each, and about 92 percent of residents had not moved in the past year. Of adults 25 and older, 83.4 percent finished high school and 15.7 percent hold a bachelor's degree or more. About 55.3 percent of residents 16 and over are in the labor force, and the typical commute is 24.6 minutes.

The county counts 1,211 veterans, 253 employer businesses and 2,904 paid jobs in 2023, and 115 building permits were issued in 2025. Persons without health insurance under 65 stand at 15.7 percent, and 13.6 percent of residents under 65 report a disability. Retail sales were about $133 million in 2022, or $7,303 per resident. For context on pricing, the Census median owner-occupied value is $131,600 and median gross rent is $782 a month.

More questions about Berrien County, GA Property Tax Guide

When does Berrien County want its property tax?

November 15 each year covers real estate and business personal property, on a schedule used since 2018. Mobile homes fall due April 1.

What does overdue Berrien County tax cost?

Interest is 1% a month from the due date, and a 10% penalty follows if 90 days pass without payment.

Where is the Berrien County tax office?

At 201 N. Davis Street, Suite 105, Nashville, inside the Administration Building, with phone (229) 686-7461 and weekday hours from 8 to 5.

How fast must a Berrien County assessment appeal be filed?

Inside 45 days from the date printed on the assessment notice. The appeal goes to the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator.

Does the Berrien tax bill go to my lender?

No. The commissioner mails statements to homeowners only. If your lender escrows, forward the bill or confirm the servicer is paying it.

Bibb County by the numbers

What does the Macon-Bibb County government do with property tax?

The city of Macon and Bibb County became a single consolidated government on January 1, 2014, following a July 31, 2012 referendum that passed in both jurisdictions. A mayor elected countywide and a nine-member commission elected by district now run it, and the small city of Payne was folded in during 2015. For property owners that means a single local government, one county school district and one tax commissioner for the whole county.

The Tax Commissioner's office is at 188 Third Street, Macon, Georgia 31201, staffed on weekdays from eight to five, with a main line of (478) 621-6500 and the email address taxinfo@maconbibb.us. It mails statements, builds the annual tax digest for the state, and distributes receipts among the State of Georgia, the county government and the school board. Values come from a separate Board of Tax Assessors at (478) 621-6701.

  • Tax Commissioner: statements, payments, liens, tax sales, excess funds claims.
  • Tax Assessors: values, returns, homestead applications, appeal filings.
  • Solid Waste Department: the garbage fee that appears alongside the property bill.

What is the Macon-Bibb housing market like for a seller?

Bibb is the largest county in the Macon metro area, with about 250 square miles of land along the Ocmulgee River. I-16, I-75 and I-475 cross it, and Lake Tobesofkee, west of downtown, has three county parks. Ocmulgee National Monument preserves Mississippian mound sites along the river. Every address falls in the Bibb County School District, and buses run through the Macon Transit Authority.

Bibb recorded 157,346 people in 2020 and is estimated at 157,556 as of July 2025. Tenure is almost evenly divided. The 2020 census put owners and renters at exactly 50 percent each, and the later survey shows owners at 51.4 percent. Because so many homes are rented, remember that the statement goes to the titleholder on January 1, never the tenant.

Census figures show 72,122 housing units in 2025 and 59,921 households. The median owner-occupied value is $174,500, median rent is $1,066 a month, median household income is $51,234 and 23.4 percent of residents are in poverty.

When are Macon-Bibb property taxes billed and due?

Bibb mails real and personal property statements by mid-September and splits the bill in two. One half is due October 15, the other November 15. Weekend dates slide to the following business day.

The January 1 owner of record is billed first. Should the office hear about a transfer during the 90 days before a due date, it verifies the change and bills the new owner. Lenders get a data file of amounts due, while the paper statement goes to the owner. Even with escrow, the owner remains the person responsible if a payment is missed.

Mobile homes run on their own track: statements by January 30, payment by April 1, and a decal issued once tax is paid. A late mobile home account carries the state penalty, 10 percent of the tax or $5 if that is more, along with monthly interest.

Macon-Bibb billing calendar, as published on the Tax Commissioner site

Can I pay late or in pieces in Macon-Bibb County?

  • Partial payments are accepted, and interest and penalties keep accruing on the rest.
  • Mail payments need a USPS date stamp to count as on time.
  • Delinquent accounts are best paid in person once a levy has begun.

The commissioner takes partial payments, as many as you like, though whatever stays unpaid keeps gathering penalties and interest. A mailed payment is on time if it bears a USPS date stamp, and a postage meter date does not qualify. On delinquent accounts the office urges delivering payment by hand, particularly after a levy and sale notice have started.

A FiFa lien is preceded by a notice of intent, mailed to the owner with 30 days to pay in full. The lien itself goes on the General Execution Docket kept by the Clerk of Superior Court, and the office says it can be recorded when a balance stays open past 90 days. Paying the tax along with fees, penalties and interest cancels it. Liens are never sold at the counter, and the office states that it does not report to credit bureaus.

The county also bills every residential premises, occupied or vacant, for garbage service through the Solid Waste Department, on a quarterly schedule. That fee serves a different purpose from the property tax, and if you appeal the value of your property the garbage fee is due in full anyway. A household below the federal poverty guidelines can request an exemption, with the application due at the Solid Waste Department by 5 p.m. each November 1.

How is homestead obtained in Macon-Bibb County?

Homestead approvals come from the Tax Assessors. Ownership and residence on January 1 are required, and paperwork received before April 1 counts for the current year. An approved owner is not asked to renew every year, yet a move or a deed change calls for a fresh application.

Exemption amounts come from state law and local acts, so the dollar figure on your bill is what matters. Ask the assessors at (478) 621-6701 what exemption your account carries and whether you qualify for any senior relief.

How is a Macon-Bibb County value appealed?

Put the appeal in writing, send it to the Board of Tax Assessors inside 45 days of the notice, and name the appeal method you want. Valid grounds include taxability, value, uniformity and a denied exemption. The Tax Commissioner is an independently elected office that neither supervises nor answers to the assessors, so appeal questions belong with the assessors.

Mobile home owners get a later cutoff: 45 days after the bill is mailed or April 1, whichever falls last. State guidance allows three years after payment to claim back tax that was collected in error or unlawfully.

What happens to a Macon-Bibb house sold for unpaid tax?

With a FiFa in place, the parcel can be levied on and sold. Auctions take place on the first Tuesday of months when one is scheduled, at 11 a.m. on the courthouse steps at 206 7th Street, and bidders have to attend personally. Bidding opens at the tax plus penalties and fees. The buyer receives a sheriff's tax deed rather than the land, and must pay within two hours using cash, certified funds or a money order.

A right of redemption survives the sale. For a year, the owner or any interested party can buy the tax deed back, paying the winning bid, taxes the buyer covered later, special assessments and a 20 percent premium. Only after that year can the buyer start foreclosing the right, by certified mail and notice in the newspaper for four straight weeks. A winning bid above the amount owed turns into excess funds, which the office holds, with lienholders ahead of the record owner. Paying the tax out of sale proceeds before a levy keeps a house out of that process entirely.

The first installment falls on October 15 and the second on November 15, after statements are mailed by September 15. Weekend dates slide to the following business day.

Does Macon-Bibb accept partial tax payments?

Yes, in as many payments as you need. Interest and penalties continue on the unpaid balance, which can eventually be subject to a lien.

What is the appeal deadline for a Macon-Bibb assessment?

The window is 45 days from the notice date, and the appeal is filed in writing with the Board of Tax Assessors. Appeal help is at (478) 621-6701.

Where do I get a copy of my Bibb County deed?

The Clerk of Superior Court deed room in the courthouse at 601 Mulberry Street, Macon, GA 31201, holds warranty deed copies.

Is a postmark accepted for Macon-Bibb tax payments?

Yes, a USPS-dated postmark proves a timely current-year payment, but a postage meter date does not.

What is Brantley County, Georgia, like?

Brantley County is a rural county in southeast Georgia with its seat at Nahunta. It spreads over roughly 442 square miles of dry ground, with the Satilla River running through it, according to Wikipedia. Georgia voters approved the county's creation on November 2, 1920, carving it from parts of Charlton, Pierce and Wayne counties.

Census QuickFacts shows 18,021 residents in 2020 and about 18,936 by mid-2025. It also reports 8,537 housing units, homes worth a median $99,600 and 79.9 percent owner occupancy over the 2020 to 2024 survey period (Census QuickFacts). Just 77 building permits were issued in 2025, which tells you new construction is thin. Most sellers are longtime owners of a single-family house, a tract of land or a mobile home.

Who runs property tax in Brantley County?

The Brantley County Government Annex, 10405 Main Street North in Nahunta, houses both offices. One sends and collects the bills, and the other decides what each parcel is worth. The rate itself is set by elected boards, so neither office can lower it.

The county's tax offices page lists both numbers, and the commissioner's own site at brantleytax.com and the assessor's site at qpublic.net give the details below.

The commissioner's site says the office moved into the annex and now has a drive-through lane. Mailing address changes for a tax bill can be requested from the property record on that site.

What does the Brantley County tax commissioner bill?

According to its website, the commissioner's office is responsible for ad valorem tax on these kinds of property:

  • Real property, meaning land and buildings
  • Personal property

You can search any parcel and pay online through the same site. The site's news page carries tax sale notices, a list of excess funds and the office's holiday closings. Look there before you list a home with unpaid years on it, since a parcel headed to tax sale is a hard sell.

The due date for the annual bill is printed on the bill itself. If yours is missing, phone 912-462-5723 and request both the due date and the amount needed to clear the account.

Keep a printout of the paid receipt for every year you own the property. Whoever handles the closing will want to see that earlier years are clear, and a receipt from the commissioner answers that at once.

How are homes valued in Brantley County?

The assessor's website reports that every schedule was updated in 2025 along with a full re-evaluation of all properties. The office keeps files on 13,406 real property parcels, 602 personal property accounts and 2,346 mobile homes without a homestead exemption.

Assessed value in Georgia is 40 percent of what a property was worth on January 1. Returns are taken from January 1 until April 1, per the assessor's site. An owner who files no return gets an assessment notice in mid-May, and that notice starts the appeal clock.

  • Submit a return before April 1 if you want to declare your own value.
  • Open the notice as soon as it arrives and note the date it carries.
  • Phone the assessor at 912-462-5251 with any questions while time remains.

Because the re-evaluation changed values across the county, a home that looked cheap on paper a few years ago may now carry a noticeably different assessment. Pull the current record before you set a sale price.

Before listing, compare the county's record of your house with what is really there. Wrong square footage, a shed that was torn down or an addition that was never recorded are easier to fix before a buyer's appraiser spots them.

What is the process for challenging a Brantley County assessment?

The assessment notice opens a 45-day window, and the assessor's site warns that you get only that one. A challenge starts with the Board of Tax Assessors. Georgia's usual path then moves to the Board of Equalization and last to Superior Court, and arbitration is offered in place of the board hearing.

Grounds are value, uniformity and taxability. Complaints about the size of the bill do not count, since the bill follows the millage rate, which cannot be appealed.

  • Write the appeal out and keep your own copy.
  • Collect recent nearby sales and any repair quotes.
  • Ask the assessor how a hearing is requested.

The count runs from the notice date, so a mailbox you rarely check can cost you days.

What do the local housing numbers say to a Brantley County seller?

Brantley is thinly settled: density was 40.7 per square mile in the 2020 count, and 99.3 percent of residents lived in rural areas. Buyers tend to be local, and many properties are big lots or mobile home sites. QuickFacts lists 6,599 households, and 94.3 percent of residents had not moved in the past year, so listings are scarce and owners stay put (Census QuickFacts).

Median gross rent is $755, and a mortgaged owner spends a median $1,087 monthly; both are the lowest figures among the four counties compared. Three practical points follow for anyone weighing a sale:

  • Family and inherited land is common, so check whose names appear on the deed and on the tax bill before you list.
  • Brantley is part of the Brunswick metropolitan area, and Wayne, Glynn, Camden, Charlton, Ware and Pierce counties touch it, so buyers often shop those neighbors too.
  • Nearly 19 percent of residents are 65 or older (19.1 percent in QuickFacts), so estate and heir questions come up often. After an owner's death, ask the probate court how to proceed.

What should a Brantley County seller do about tax owed at closing?

Begin by getting a payoff amount from the tax commissioner, because unpaid county taxes must be cleared before a buyer can receive clean title. Then have the settlement agent work out each side's share of the year's bill.

If the house is a mobile home, confirm whether it is billed on its own or together with the land, since the assessor tracks non-homesteaded mobile homes as separate accounts. Homestead status affects this, so ask the assessor which treatment your home has.

Owners hurt by the Highway 82 fire can call the county commissioners' office at 912-462-5256, extension 5, about the recovery resources on the county website. Ask the assessor how fire damage is reflected in your record before you price the property.

More questions about Brantley County, GA Property Tax Guide

How can I pay my Brantley County tax bill?

Pay the tax commissioner, either online at brantleytax.com or in person at Suite D of the Government Annex, 10405 Main Street North, Nahunta. The office number is 912-462-5723, and it posts weekday hours of 8:00 to 4:30.

What is the appeal deadline for a Brantley County assessment?

The deadline is 45 days after the date printed on the notice. The assessor's website treats that window as firm, so file in writing before it ends.

Does the Brantley County assessor set my tax bill?

No. The assessor sets the value only. The county commissioners and the school board set millage rates, and the tax commissioner sends the bill.

Can I sell a Brantley County house if taxes are unpaid?

Yes, provided the back taxes are paid at or before closing so the buyer gets clear title. Request a payoff from the tax commissioner and make sure it appears on the settlement statement.

When are Brantley County property tax returns due?

Returns are taken from January 1 until April 1 each year. Owners who miss that cutoff receive assessment notices in mid-May, and the 45-day appeal period starts then.
