Clarke County by the numbers

How is Athens-Clarke County property tax organized?

Clarke County and the City of Athens operate as one government, so the Athens-Clarke County Property Tax Division handles the bill for the whole county. Its page explains that the money supports the Clarke County Board of Education, Athens-Clarke County and the State of Georgia.

Real estate and business personal property taxes are generally due by October 20. If a bill goes unpaid, the property can be levied on and eventually sold. The division describes a 5% penalty added every 120 days past the due date, up to four times, for a possible total of 20%, on top of interest.

  • Land and buildings are taxed where they are located, per O.C.G.A. 48-5-11.
  • Taxable value is set at 40% of market value, with exceptions written into law (O.C.G.A. 48-5-7).
  • Standing timber escapes tax until it is sold or cut, then it is taxed at 100% of its fair market value.

Each bill shows both the fair market value and the assessed value, so you can see what the assessors used before you decide whether to appeal.

What sets Clarke County apart from the rest of Georgia?

Clarke is Georgia's smallest county by area, at 121 square miles including 1.8 of water. It lies in the Piedmont and drains mostly to the Upper Oconee River. The General Assembly carved it out of Jackson County on December 5, 1801 and named it for Elijah Clarke. Watkinsville served as seat until November 1871, when county offices moved to Athens. Athens and Winterville are the cities, and the town of Bogart lies mostly in Oconee County.

Its mills and railroad, which reached Athens in 1841, made it second only to Savannah and Chatham County in manufacturing investment during the 1840s. Today the University of Georgia shapes the housing market. Census QuickFacts counts 129,921 people for 2025, just 1.0% above the 2020 base, and households average 2.19 people with 16.1% of residents under 18.

Just 41.4% of homes are lived in by their owners, the lowest share among the four Georgia counties compared on QuickFacts, and typical rent is $1,219. An owner-held home has a middle value of $298,900, the middle household income is $53,625, and 73.5% of people stayed at the same address over the prior year. Many Athens houses are therefore rentals, and investor-owned homes receive the same bill as any other.

What are the steps to contest an Athens-Clarke County value?

Put the appeal in writing to the Board of Assessors, with 45 days counted from the mailing of the assessment notice. If the assessors leave the value alone, the file moves to the Board of Equalization on its own. The Athens-Clarke assessors answer questions at 706-613-3140.

Appeal timeline posted by Athens-Clarke County and the Georgia Department of Revenue
StepTiming
Written appeal delivered to the assessors45 days from notice mailing
Board of Equalization notifies both sides of hearing date15 days after the appeal reaches that board
Hearing held20 to 30 days after that letter
Appeal to Superior CourtWritten, 30 days after the Board of Equalization rules

At the hearing the Board of Assessors' appraiser presents comparable sales first, then you present your evidence, the Board of Equalization asks questions, and a ruling is sent to both sides. Arbitration and a hearing officer are the other two methods the state allows, and the assessors' office can explain them.

Which returns must Athens-Clarke County owners file?

Form PT-50R, the real estate return, goes to the tax commissioner in room 250 of the Courthouse before the April 1 close of the filing season, in any year the property was acquired or altered. If nothing affecting value has changed since last year, you may skip it. A taxpayer who fails to file a required return faces a 10% penalty on the value not returned, plus interest and possibly other penalties.

Personal property follows a stricter rule. Form PT-50P goes to the Board of Assessors every April 1 whether or not anything changed. The tax commissioner also warns buyers of businesses, boats and aircraft to check for unpaid personal property tax before closing, since attorneys usually search real estate taxes only.

What exemptions and refunds exist for Athens-Clarke County owners?

Georgia's state homestead exemption goes to people who own and occupy a home as their primary residence, and the Department of Revenue's page for Clarke County confirms that an application can be made at any time but must be in by April 1 of the first year the exemption is sought. Failing to apply counts as a waiver. Some counties add larger local exemptions, so ask the Athens-Clarke County offices which ones apply to a given house before you assume the standard amount is all there is.

Taxpayers can also ask in writing for a refund of tax that was erroneously or illegally assessed and collected, as long as the request starts within three years of payment. When an assessment is under appeal and the final taxable value comes in lower, the refund is processed automatically once that value is final. Equipment, machinery and fixtures used by a business are assessed at 40% of fair market value, and the assessor may value a going business as a whole.

What happens if taxes go unpaid in Athens-Clarke County?

Athens-Clarke County runs its own tax sales. The tax commissioner serves as ex officio sheriff, and Georgia law requires the property to be advertised for four consecutive weeks in the legal section of the county newspaper, which the county identifies as the Athens Banner-Herald.

  • Sales begin at 10:00 a.m. on the first Tuesday of the month, ordinarily in front of the courthouse, and run as a public outcry auction.
  • The opening bid equals the taxes due plus costs, and the property goes to the highest bidder or may be bid in for the county.
  • Payment is due at the sale, by cashier's or certified check from an FDIC-insured institution.
  • The tax commissioner then executes and records a tax deed. The purchaser owes taxes as they come due, and any amount paid may be added to the redemption price.

An owner who sees a notice for their address should contact the tax commissioner at once. Redemption rights exist under Georgia law, and the county's tax sale page has the current list of properties.

What should I settle at closing when selling in Clarke County?

Tax for the full year falls on the person who held title in January, and Georgia refunds nothing for months after a sale. Any credit for the stretch a buyer will own the home is worked out between the parties on the closing statement.

State guidance also gives taxpayers 60 days from the bill's postmark before interest starts. When the October 20 date has gone by with a balance still open, request a payoff figure with penalties included and pay it out of sale proceeds so the title is clear.

Rental owners selling an occupied house should confirm that business personal property, such as appliances listed on a business return, has no balance. Questions about exemptions, returns or values go to the assessors, and bills and payments go to the Property Tax Division.

More questions about Clarke County, GA Property Tax Guide

What is the Athens-Clarke County due date?

October 20 in the usual case. The Property Tax Division lists that date for real estate and business personal property.

What is the Athens-Clarke County appeal window?

It is 45 days from the day the assessment notice was mailed. Send the appeal in writing to the Board of Assessors, and call 706-613-3140 with questions.

Who conducts tax sales in Clarke County?

The tax commissioner, acting as ex officio sheriff. Auctions start at 10:00 a.m. on each month's first Tuesday, usually in front of the courthouse.

Must I file a property return every year in Athens-Clarke County?

Not for real estate if nothing changed. Real estate returns are due January 1 to April 1 in years the property changed or was acquired, while personal property returns are due every April 1.

Do most Clarke County residents own their homes?

No. QuickFacts shows owners living in 41.4% of homes for 2020 to 2024, so renters are the majority.

Who to contact in Clayton County

Clayton County by the numbers

Who bills and who values property in Clayton County?

Two separate Clayton County offices touch every parcel. Value comes from the Board of Tax Assessors. The bill, the collection and the split of the money among the county, the cities, fire services and the school board come from the Tax Commissioner. Neither office picks the millage rate: the Board of Commissioners picks the county's, and the other taxing bodies pick theirs.

You will find both under one roof in the Jonesboro government complex on South McDonough Street (number 121). The assessors are on the fourth floor of Annex 3, phone (770) 477-3285. The Tax Commissioner is on the second floor of the same annex, and the property tax line is (770) 477-3311. Knowing which door to knock on saves a seller days, because a value question sent to the commissioner or a payoff question sent to the assessors simply gets redirected.

Value is fixed as of January 1. A house sold in October still shows up on the bill under whoever held it on that January date, so the bill and the closing statement have to be read side by side.

What should a seller know about Clayton County itself?

Clayton County is a compact, heavily built-up county south of Atlanta. At 144 square miles, only two Georgia counties are smaller. Jonesboro holds the courthouse, Forest Park is the biggest city, and Clayton State University is in Morrow. The county also holds most of Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport.

The 2020 census counted 297,595 residents, 106,200 households and 114,038 housing units, with 6.9% of those units vacant. Renters edged out owners in 2020, at 50.5% of occupied homes to 49.5%, and the median age was 34.3. A landlord selling with tenants in place is a common situation here, and the lease is one more item to settle before a closing date.

The county sits across two river basins, with the eastern side between Forest Park and Lovejoy draining toward the Ocmulgee and the western side toward the Flint. Interstates 75, 85, 285 and 675 all cross it, along with US 19/41 (Tara Boulevard) and State Routes 54, 85 and 138. Conley and Irondale are census-designated places, and Ellenwood, Rex and Mountain View are unincorporated communities. Ask the Tax Commissioner whether your parcel also carries a city bill.

When are Clayton County property tax bills due?

The Tax Commissioner's own presentation describes a yearly rhythm. Assessment notices go out in spring or early summer, the millage rate process runs from about mid July to mid August, and bills follow around mid September, with a due date usually in mid November. The presentation puts the payment window at 60 days after mail-out. Those dates shift each year, and the printed bill and the office line, (770) 477-3311, give the real ones.

If your value is under appeal when bills go out, you receive two bills. One covers 85% and falls due with everyone else's. The other covers the remaining 15% and comes due, or comes back as a refund, after the appeal settles. Request a copy of both before you list the house.

The state revenue department's county fact sheet adds two statewide rules. Interest waits until 60 days after the bill's postmark, though penalties can follow on delinquent balances. A claim for tax assessed in error has to begin within three years of payment, and appeal refunds are issued once the final value is set.

What can I do if my Clayton County value looks too high?

The clock is 45 days, counted from the mailing date shown on the notice, and the appeal has to be written. Homestead applications and other specialized assessment requests ride on that same date. A late filing forfeits that year's challenge. File with the assessors in Annex 3, or through the county's online appeals site.

After the first review, the notice names four routes.

Appeal routes listed on the Clayton County notice of assessment (Clayton County Board of Tax Assessors)
RouteWhat it can decideCondition printed on the notice
Board of EqualizationValue, uniformity, exemptions or taxabilityOpen to any owner who files in time
Nonbinding arbitrationValue onlyRequires a certified appraisal
Hearing officerValue or uniformityReal property that is not a homestead and is valued above $500,000, plus large personal property accounts
Superior CourtAs agreedOnly by written agreement with the assessors

Within 10 business days of a request, the assessors owe you the records behind your value, so ask early. Comparable sales and photos of defects the county could not see from the road make the usual evidence. The rate itself is off the table, since an appeal reaches value, uniformity and taxability only.

Which exemptions can a Clayton County homeowner claim?

A homestead is the one house you own and occupy as your primary residence on January 1, and nobody can hold two. Applications go to the Tax Commissioner. The county says it takes them all year, but the filing window is January 2 to April 1 and a late one waits for the following year. After approval the exemption renews itself, and the owner's only duty is to report a loss of eligibility.

A local base-year homestead measure was prepared for Clayton voters on the November 4, 2025 ballot. As the commissioner's office described it, the measure would freeze the county-purposes value for tax years 2026 through 2030 for these groups:

  • Residents age 65 or older
  • Disabled veterans
  • Unremarried surviving spouses of peace officers or firefighters killed in the line of duty
  • Residents who are 100 percent disabled

Ask the commissioner's office whether your parcel is covered.

A homestead exemption follows the occupant. A buyer files separately after moving in, so the next bill on the house can run higher than yours did.

What happens if taxes go unpaid on a Clayton County house?

Unpaid taxes lead to an execution on the property and, eventually, a tax sale. The Tax Commissioner's property portal links to tax sale notices for the October 2026 and November 2026 sales, a bidder pre-registration form, and an excess funds claim form for owners owed money after a sale. Those links show how active the process is in a county this size.

A tax sale transfers a tax deed and not clear title, and Georgia law gives the owner a right to redeem. A house with a tax lien on it is hard to finance. Lenders want the account clear, and the closing office will deduct any balance from your proceeds. If you are behind, call (770) 477-3311 first and ask what it takes to clear the account by your target closing date.

How are property taxes handled when you sell in Clayton County?

The county does not split the year between buyer and seller. That split lives in your sales contract and settlement statement, which the closing attorney prepares. Have the closing office request a payoff covering the county bill and any city bill.

  • Pull your current bill from the Tax Commissioner's portal and note whether a city bill also applies.
  • Ask whether an appeal is pending, because a pending appeal means a second bill for the remaining 15%.
  • Confirm any homestead exemption will be removed after the sale.
  • Keep the closing statement. It is your record that the bill was paid.

A sale with tenants or a repair list can still close on a cash timeline, so weigh any written cash offer against what a listing would net.

More questions about Clayton County, GA Property Tax Guide

What is the filing deadline for a Clayton County value appeal?

The deadline is 45 days after the mailing date on your notice, and the appeal must be in writing. Take it to the assessors at 121 S. McDonough Street, Annex 3, fourth floor, in Jonesboro, or use the county's online appeals site. A late one leaves the value standing for the year.

Which Clayton County office answers bill questions, and which handles values?

Bills, payments, exemptions and payoffs go to the Tax Commissioner at (770) 477-3311. Values, notices and appeals go to the assessors at (770) 477-3285. The assessors collect nothing, and the commissioner changes no values.

Do I pay anything while a Clayton County appeal is pending?

Yes, most of it. A parcel under appeal receives two bills. The 85% bill is due on the usual date. The other 15% is settled after the decision, and that can mean a small balance or a refund.

Can a Clayton County house with unpaid taxes still be sold?

Yes. Back taxes come out of your proceeds at the closing table, so get a payoff figure for the closing date. A parcel already sold at a tax sale needs one more step, because the tax deed buyer holds an interest until redemption. Start with a call to (770) 477-3311.

Does my homestead exemption pass to the buyer of my Clayton County house?

No. The exemption belongs to the person who lives in the home. A buyer files a new application with the Tax Commissioner, and one filed after April 1 is processed for the following year.

Who to contact in Cobb County

What we confirmed on official pages

  • Bills mailed by August 15; payment due October 15 (received or USPS-postmarked); 2026 bills issued Aug 19, due Oct 15
  • Late payments: 5% penalty plus monthly interest; fi fa fee $23 on taxes under $100 or $33 over $100; late fees cannot be waived

Cobb County by the numbers

Who sends the property tax bill in Cobb County?

County and school taxes arrive in one bill from the Cobb County Tax Commissioner, who collects for the Board of Commissioners and the school district. A parcel outside city limits stops there. A parcel in Acworth, Austell, Kennesaw, Mableton, Marietta, Smyrna or Powder Springs also gets a city bill, since each of those seven cities collects for itself.

Values are not the commissioner's call. Each year the Board of Tax Assessors sets fair market value, and Georgia taxes 40% of it. The overview page writes the formula as (Fair Market Value x 0.40) x (Millage Rate / 1,000), where one mill is $1 per $1,000 of assessed value. County, school and city authorities choose their rates annually.

The 2026 digest produced 270,574 bills worth $1,363,609,369, according to the county's announcement. Real property accounted for 256,894 of them and personal property for 13,680. Eligible homesteads also received the state's Homeowner Tax Relief Grant for 2026, which appears as a reduction on the bill apart from any exemption.

When is Cobb County property tax due?

Bills go out by August 15 and fall due October 15. Collection cannot start until the tax digest is approved, normally in mid to late July, so nobody can prepay. The 2026 bills were issued in mid August and were due October 15, 2026.

Money is on time if the office has it, or if the envelope bears a Postal Service postmark dated by midnight on October 15. Meter and kiosk stamps do not count. A bill that has not shown up by August 30 can be printed from the commissioner's website, and its absence does not excuse penalty or interest.

The office takes partial payments, yet whatever remains after October 15 is charged a 5% penalty and monthly interest. Arrangements start with a call to 770-528-8600. A returned check costs $30 or 5%, whichever is greater, plus bank charges.

Where and how can you pay a Cobb County tax bill?

Owners have these choices:

  • Online by e-check or card, with no convenience fee on e-check
  • Phone, at 1-866-535-2622
  • Mail, to P.O. Box 100127, Marietta, GA 30061
  • In person or by drop box at the offices below

The county says it keeps none of the card fees.

Cobb County Tax Commissioner in-person payment locations (Cobb County Tax Commissioner)
OfficeAddress
Main Property Tax Division736 Whitlock Avenue, Marietta
East Cobb4400 Lower Roswell Road, Marietta
South Cobb4700 Austell Road, Austell
North Cobb2932 Canton Road, Marietta
West Cobb3858 Kemp Ridge Road, Acworth

Escrow accounts work like this: once a lender tells the office it pays your taxes, the bill goes to both of you, and you remain responsible for confirming it was paid. A double payment is refunded. The coupon is optional as long as the parcel ID is written on the check.

What if I disagree with my Cobb County valuation?

A value dispute is filed in writing with the Board of Tax Assessors within 45 days of the notice date, and the commissioner has no say. The grounds are value, uniformity and taxability, never the millage rate. Cases the assessors do not resolve go on to the Board of Equalization.

Filing an appeal does not move the due date. The bill for a parcel under appeal carries a lower appeal amount, set at 85% of assessed value or 100% of the prior uncontested value, and at least that much must be paid by October 15 to avoid the 5% penalty. Interest of up to $150 a month can accrue on the remainder; paying the full bill by the due date avoids it.

The commissioner's 2026 estimator runs on 2025 millage rates and covers county tax alone, leaving out city tax and special classifications. A second version for new home buyers lets you enter a market value, a tax district and exemptions. Whatever it shows, the official bill controls.

What homestead exemptions and relief can a Cobb County owner use?

The basic homestead exemption goes to owners living in the house as their primary residence on January 1. Seniors can claim more starting at age 62, including a full or reduced school tax exemption. Other exemptions cover 100% service-connected disabled veterans, disabled owners, surviving spouses of certain public servants, nonprofits and religious organizations.

File online, in person or by mail, with the application received or postmarked before the appeal deadline on your assessment notice. Anything later is processed for the next year. If you held an exemption elsewhere, include a letter showing it was removed. A rental cannot carry a homestead, and an owner who keeps one after becoming ineligible owes penalties and interest on the taxes saved.

A marriage, divorce, death or ownership change calls for a fresh application backed by a recorded deed, marriage certificate or divorce decree. Special classifications such as conservation use, historic property and forest land go through the assessors.

What happens when Cobb County taxes go unpaid?

Once the due date passes, the office sends a written notice, and 30 days later it may issue a Fi. Fa., a tax execution that works as a lien. The Fi. Fa. brings a $23 charge on taxes under $100 or $33 on taxes over $100, plus administrative costs. Late fees are never waived.

A sale takes place on the first Tuesday of any month where one is scheduled, at Superior Court Plaza on the corner of Haynes Street and Washington Avenue. Bidding runs from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m., in person only, after pre-registration, and winners pay with cash or a certified check. What is sold is the tax deed, never a tax lien. Redemption stays open for 12 months, and the price adds the bid, any later taxes the buyer paid, special assessments, and a premium of 20% for the first year or fraction and 10% for each year after.

  • Get a written payoff before listing.
  • A filed Fi. Fa. adds its fee to the payoff.
  • After a tax sale, redemption stays open for 12 months.

How are Cobb County taxes handled when you sell?

Proration is not something the commissioner does. A full year of tax is figured on the parcel, responsibility is sorted out when the sale closes, and your closing paperwork says who pays. The tax follows the property, so whoever owns it at the time should make sure it is paid.

Afterward, report the ownership change to the commissioner and have your homestead exemption removed. The new owner files for theirs under the rules above. A house with tenants, repairs or a delinquent bill can still move, and the payoff comes out of proceeds either way.

More questions about Cobb County, GA Property Tax Guide

What date do Cobb County property taxes come due?

October 15, with bills mailed by August 15. The 2026 bills fell due October 15, 2026. A payment counts if it arrives or is postmarked by the Postal Service by then, and what is left afterward draws a 5% penalty plus monthly interest.

Does Cobb County allow installment payments?

Partial payments are taken, and interest and penalty still build on the balance after October 15. Arrange payments by calling 770-528-8600. An appeal does not defer payment, though only the appeal amount is required by the due date.

Will Cobb County split the tax bill between me and the buyer?

No, the office stays out of it. The bill covers the whole year, and your closing paperwork decides each side's share. The closing attorney or title company usually pays from proceeds.

What if my Cobb County tax bill never arrived?

The tax is still owed, and penalty and interest stand. Print the bill from the commissioner's website, pay with the parcel ID on your check, or call 770-528-8600. A corrected mailing address prevents a repeat.

How long can an owner redeem after a Cobb County tax sale?

Twelve months from the sale. The owner, a creditor or anyone else with an interest may redeem by paying the bid, later taxes, special assessments and the stepped premium of 20% then 10%. The buyer calculates the exact figure.

Coffee County by the numbers

What should sellers know about Coffee County's size and housing?

Coffee County lies in south Georgia's Wiregrass region, and Douglas serves as its seat and its biggest city. The legislature created the county in 1854. It spans 603 square miles, 575 of them land, and holds three other incorporated cities: Ambrose, Broxton and Nicholls. South Georgia State College, the University System's oldest two-year school, is in Douglas.

The 2020 census found 43,092 people in 15,277 households and a median age of 36.6. Of the 17,331 housing units, 11.9% stood vacant. Among occupied homes, owners held 63.9% and renters 36.1%. Sellers with acreage should look at the land programs described below before they list.

Local landmarks include the Broxton Rocks sandstone outcrops, General Coffee State Park at 1,490 acres, and Mule Day, held the second Saturday in November.

Where do Coffee County's two tax offices sit?

Two offices share the job. Values and appeals belong to the Coffee County Tax Assessors Office, at 224 West Ashley Street, Suite C, in Douglas. It keeps weekday hours from 8:00 to 5:00 and answers at 912-384-2136, with a separate personal property line, 912-493-1100.

Billing, collection and homestead applications sit with the Tax Commissioner, next door in Suite B at 224 Ashley Street West. Weekday hours run from 8:00 to 4:50, and the phone is (912) 384-4895. Mail goes to P.O. Box 1207, Douglas, GA 31533. Online payment runs through the commissioner's site, which sits on a vendor's platform. Bill questions belong here, because the assessors' page says they establish values only.

Georgia cities levy their own ad valorem tax, and in some counties the Tax Commissioner collects it on the same bill. Ask the Tax Commissioner whether a parcel in Douglas, Broxton, Nicholls or Ambrose gets one bill or two.

What are the key property tax deadlines in Coffee County?

The assessors' page prints the dates owners need most. April 1 closes filing for homestead exemptions, personal property returns and the conservation use, preferential and forest land programs, though those applications are also taken during the appeal window. Eligibility is measured on January 1, when you must still own and live in the home.

Coffee County filing and appeal dates printed by the Tax Assessors Office
ItemDate
Homestead exemption filingJanuary 1 to April 1
Personal property returnApril 1
Conservation use, preferential and forest land applicationsApril 1, or during the appeal window
2026 assessment notices mailedAugust 4, 2026
2026 appeal deadlineSeptember 18, 2026 (passed)

A review of every parcel is also under way, spread over three years, with contract appraisers from GMASS who wear ID badges and drive marked vehicles. The assessors give notice that appraisers will visit parcels sold in the last 12 months or tied to a building permit, a value return, fire damage, demolition or an appeal. Most field visits fall between January 1 and May 1.

What is the route for challenging a Coffee County value?

Forty-five days from the notice date is the rule, and it explains the 2026 window of August 4 to September 18. Owners of real property are urged to use the appeals module on the county's qPublic site, with lobby computers for anyone who prefers to file in person. Personal property appeals go on paper, with a postmark by the deadline if mailed.

The assessors review each appeal first. A value the assessors keep goes to a Board of Equalization hearing, and an owner still unhappy afterward can take the case to Superior Court. Arbitration can stand in for that hearing. Valid grounds are taxability, value and uniformity with similar properties. The size of the bill is not one of them.

A notice that never arrived is a reason to call the assessors and confirm the mailing address on file, since their page says what they give you then counts as the official notice.

What exemptions and programs does Coffee County list?

For homestead, apply at the Tax Commissioner's office between New Year's Day and April 1 of the year you first want relief. Approval carries forward every year until ownership changes or you switch to a different kind. The county's exemptions page lists:

  • A standard homestead exemption.
  • A $4,000 exemption for owners 65 or older.
  • A school tax exemption for owners 62 or older under the income limit printed on the page, capped at $10,000 of assessed value.
  • A $50,000 exemption for qualifying disabled veterans, extended to an unremarried surviving spouse or minor children.
  • A deferral program for homestead owners 62 and older with gross income of $15,000 or less. Deferred tax is due when ownership changes or when the deferred amount plus interest reaches 85% of the property's fair market value.

State law can change those amounts, so confirm each with the Tax Commissioner before relying on it. In years when the legislature funds the Homeowners Tax Relief Grant, it appears as a credit on the bill.

Landowners have their own options. Some farmland is assessed at 30% of market value where the usual share is 40%. Conservation use assessment asks for a 10-year covenant and a $10.00 recording fee with the application. Breaking the covenant costs twice the taxes saved, plus 1% monthly interest if the break goes unreported. A buyer who keeps the same use can sign onto the covenant.

What is the Coffee County billing calendar, and what does paying late cost?

Unless a local government changes it, the state due date is December 20. A county may pick December 1, November 15 or installments, so read the date on your Coffee County bill or ask the Tax Commissioner. The state fact sheet says interest does not start until 60 days after the bill's postmark, and penalties may follow.

Tax assessed in error can be refunded if you ask in writing within three years of paying it. Appealed values refund automatically once final. Unpaid balances can end in a lien and a tax sale, and a closing office will insist they be cleared.

Land enrolled in conservation use deserves a heads-up to your closing attorney, since a buyer who changes the use can set off the penalty.

What happens to the tax bill when a Coffee County house sells?

Georgia taxes the person holding title on January 1, and your sales contract and settlement statement decide how the year is shared. Have the closing attorney request a payoff from the Tax Commissioner, (912) 384-4895, covering any city bill too. Afterward, tell the commissioner so your homestead exemption is dropped, and let the buyer know they must file their own, by April 1.

  • Confirm the current balance and whether a city bill also applies.
  • Ask whether the parcel is in conservation use, since the covenant affects a buyer.
  • Check whether a homestead exemption will need to be dropped.
  • Keep the closing statement as proof that taxes were paid.

Deferred maintenance, tenants or back taxes can slow a conventional sale, and a buyer paying cash skips the lender's appraisal.

More questions about Coffee County, GA Property Tax Guide

Which Coffee County office do I call about a tax question?

Bills, payments and homestead filings go to the Tax Commissioner at (912) 384-4895. Values and appeals go to the Tax Assessors Office at 912-384-2136. The assessors only set values, so a bill question gets redirected to the commissioner.

When must a Coffee County homestead exemption be filed?

Before April 1 of the first year you want it, while owning and living in the home on January 1. The Tax Commissioner takes the application. One filed later generally waits for the next tax year.

Did Coffee County's 2026 appeal window close?

Yes. Notices went out August 4, 2026, and the last day to appeal was September 18, 2026. Real property owners were steered to the qPublic appeals module. Future windows last 45 days from the date on the notice.

Does Coffee County conservation use transfer to a buyer?

It can. A buyer who keeps the same qualifying use and signs the covenant avoids any penalty. A change of use inside the 10-year period brings twice the taxes saved. Tell your closing attorney if the parcel is enrolled.

How does a Coffee County closing handle the tax bill?

Your proceeds cover the balance, city bill included, and the contract sets each side's share of the year. Ask the Tax Commissioner for a payoff dated to your closing.

Colquitt County by the numbers

Who mails the Colquitt County tax bill?

The Tax Commissioner in Moultrie mails and collects the bill. Value belongs to the Tax Assessor's Office, and the commissioner's own site says that office sets neither the value nor the millage rate.

The counter sits at 101 East Central Ave., Moultrie, GA 31768. The postal box is number 99. Staff work weekdays from 8:00am until 4:30pm, and the property tax line is (229) 616-7410. The same office runs motor vehicle registration, and a separate solid waste desk at 101 East Central Avenue, Office 168, is reached at (229) 616-7405. The landfill opens Saturday mornings from 8:00am to noon, which matters if you are clearing a house before listing it.

  • Tax Assessor's Office: appraisal, assessment notices and exemption approvals.
  • Board of Equalization: administrative appeals, with members named by the grand jury.
  • County commission and school board: each levies its own mill rate.
  • Tax Commissioner: bills, payments, liens and levies.

What does Colquitt County look like around Moultrie?

Colquitt County is a Southwest Georgia farming county of about 557 square miles, created on February 25, 1856. Moultrie holds the courthouse and is the biggest city, and the county's western side drains toward the Ochlockonee River while the central and eastern parts drain toward the Withlacoochee and Little River basins.

The county touches Tift, Cook, Brooks, Thomas, Mitchell and Worth counties. Gray Lake and Lake Murphy are its named lakes, and Autreyville, Barbers, Hartsfield, Murphy and Riverside are listed as unincorporated communities. In Moultrie, US 319 runs to Interstate 75 about 24 miles east, and Reed Bingham State Park and the Tom White Linear Park trail are local landmarks. The Colquitt County School District operates elementary schools named for Doerun, Funston and Norman Park.

QuickFacts reports 47,438 people in its 2025 estimate and 19,775 housing units. Owners occupy 63.7% of homes. The Census five-year estimate puts a typical owned home at $121,400, gross rent at $818 and household income at $49,341.

When do Colquitt County bills fall due?

Real estate and business personal property are normally due December 10, and the commissioner's site says bills are mailed at least 60 days before that. Follow whatever date your own bill prints, since the page warns it may change.

Tax bills are addressed to the owner, not the lender. A homeowner whose mortgage does not escrow must pass the bill along. The office also cannot promise a bill reaches you, and it says interest, penalty and costs apply regardless.

Mobile and manufactured homes follow their own deadline, and the county's two pages give different dates for it. Call the tax commissioner and ask which applies to your unit. A mobile home moving into or out of the county needs a relocation permit first, from the Compliance office in the Courthouse Annex, reached at 229-616-7417.

How are late bills handled in Colquitt County?

A bill left past the due date draws interest each month, and later a penalty. The county's pages describe the exact rates differently, so ask for a written payoff instead of working it out yourself. The site does say the penalty skips homesteaded property whose bill is under $500.

If the tax stays unpaid, a tax lien called a FiFa goes on the General Execution Docket at the Clerk of Superior Court. The site says it stays on a credit record for at least seven years, and that the commissioner may levy and eventually sell the property. It describes levy as a last resort.

The office mails delinquent notices only at certain intervals. That means the amount on the last notice you saw may be out of date by the time you pay or close.

Who owes the tax if the house sells in Colquitt County?

The January 1 owner stays on the bill and on any lien, even if the deed changes hands in June. A seller can move that to the buyer by putting the closing statement in the commissioner's hands by day 90 after the due date.

The office spells out the mechanics. If your closing prorated the tax, bring the settlement statement to the office on East Central Avenue. With that in hand it can record a lien against the new owner if the bill remains unpaid. A bill that arrives for a house you already sold should be forwarded to the buyer.

Find out from the title company how the county gets paid, then ask the commissioner for a payoff dated near the closing. Selling with a recorded lien is workable, because the payoff is settled at the closing table and comes out of the sale funds.

What exemptions and programs does Colquitt County list?

The commissioner's site lists a standard exemption and several age, veteran and income-based ones, all subtracted from the assessed value, which Georgia fixes at 40% of fair market value. The first application goes to the Tax Assessor's Office, and first-time owners are told to bring a copy of the warranty deed. Georgia requires it to be received by April 1.

  • Standard homestead: printed as $2,000 off assessed value, for county, school system and state levies.
  • Elderly school tax, age 62 or older: up to $10,000 off, with net income of $10,000 or less.
  • Elderly general, age 65 or older: up to $4,000 off, with a $10,000 income test that excludes Social Security and some retirement income.
  • Disabled veteran and qualifying surviving spouse: up to $63,780 off.
  • Floating exemption: age 62 or older with gross household income of $30,000 or less, covering state and county tax but not school tax.

Colquitt County also has local exemptions that override the state amounts when larger, so the assessors can tell you what applies today. Farmland has its own paths: assessment at 30% for bona fide agricultural use, and conservation use or timber programs that require a covenant of at least 10 years. Historic property and certain hazardous-site redevelopment parcels may also qualify. Owners 62 and older with gross household income of $15,000 or less can defer tax until a sale or until the deferral and interest reach 85% of fair market value.

How do I dispute a Colquitt County value?

Put the appeal in writing, and do it inside 45 days counted from the date on the assessment notice. The county FAQ names two routes, equalization board or arbitrator, and says either result can be carried on to Superior Court.

Each spring, up to April 1, you may also file a return stating your own opinion of the property's January 1 value. An owner who stays silent is treated as returning the same value and exemptions as the year before. For a mobile home the county page allows 45 days to appeal to the assessors, then 21 days from their notice to reach the equalization board.

At the Tax Commissioner's office, 101 East Central Ave., Moultrie. Staff work weekdays from 8:00am to 4:30pm, and the card payments carry a convenience fee from the card company.

What date is Colquitt County property tax normally due?

December 10 for real estate and business personal property. Your bill's printed date is the one to trust, because the commissioner says it may change.

Can I sell a Colquitt County house with a recorded tax lien?

Yes. The payoff is settled from the sale funds at closing, so request a current figure from the commissioner and hand it to the title company.

Which Colquitt County office takes homestead applications?

The Tax Assessor's Office. Georgia requires the application to be received by April 1, and a later filing counts toward the next tax year.

What is the appeal window for a Colquitt County assessment?

45 days counted from the date on the notice. You can ask for the equalization board or an arbitrator, and Superior Court is open afterward.

Columbia County by the numbers

Where does a Columbia County, GA homeowner deal with property tax?

Property tax in Columbia County is handled at the Tax Commissioner's Property Tax Division in Evans, 630 Ronald Reagan Drive, Building C, Second Floor, Evans, GA 30809. Call 706-261-8299 for property tax. Doors open at 8 am and close at 4:30 pm on non-holiday weekdays.

The same division takes homestead applications, runs the delinquent tax unit, and posts the county digest and a tax worksheet. Valuation sits with a separate assessment office, so a question about why your house is worth what the notice says is not a tax commissioner question. Ask the division for the right contact if you are unsure where to start.

  • Bills, payments and payoffs: Tax Commissioner, Property Tax Division.
  • Homestead applications: same office in Evans.
  • Delinquent accounts and sheriff's tax sales: Delinquent Tax Division.
  • Mobile home permits: Planning and Zoning in Evans, or city hall in Grovetown or Harlem.

What kind of county is Columbia County for someone selling a house?

Columbia County is a fast-growing suburban county on the Savannah River, part of the Augusta metropolitan area. Wikipedia gives its area as 308 square miles and lists Grovetown and Harlem as its cities, with Appling, Evans and Martinez as census-designated places. Appling is the legal county seat, while Evans is where county government actually operates.

Interstate 20 crosses the county, and US 78 and US 221 are among the other major roads. Clarks Hill Lake, also called Strom Thurmond Lake, is among the county's named waters. The Columbia County School District covers the whole county. Growth is the story here: the 2020 census counted 156,010 residents, and the latest July 2025 estimate of 169,189 is 8.4% higher.

QuickFacts lists 65,264 housing units. Owners hold 78.1% of them, the typical owned home is valued at $305,300, rent averages $1,409 and household income is $95,592. Those figures describe the county as a whole, not any one street.

How is a Columbia County tax bill built?

The county's tax worksheet page lays out the steps: fair market value times 40% gives the assessed value, and assessed value times the millage rate gives the tax. The millage rate is expressed in dollars for every thousand of assessed value, and it comes from the proposed budget divided by the tax digest, which is the total of all assessments.

Exemptions come off before the rate is applied. The county posts a downloadable tax calculation workbook labeled for estimating only, and it warns that a change in rates, values or fees changes the final amount. Use it to compare scenarios, then get the official figure from the division.

Payment can be made online through the county's pay-tax page. Credit cards carry a third-party processing fee, and an eCheck carries a $1.50 per item fee. If your lender escrows the tax, the county asks you to contact the lender first so nothing is paid twice.

Which homestead exemptions does Columbia County offer?

The county lists a regular exemption plus several age, disability and veteran exemptions, and each reduces the assessed value rather than the market value. Applications are taken at the Evans office, and the county says you must apply no later than April 1 to get the benefit for the same year. The office accepts applications year-round.

  • Regular homestead (S1): up to $10,000 off assessed value, for state, county and school purposes, excluding bond taxes and city taxes.
  • Age 62 (L3): $40,000 off for county and school, with net income of both spouses not over $15,000.
  • Local school exemption, age 70 (L6): the school tax on the home and up to three adjoining acres, no income limit.
  • Disabled veteran (S5): $126,526 off, with a VA letter showing 100% service-connected, total and permanent disability, refreshed every three years.
  • Total and permanent disability (L5): $40,000 off, with two physician affidavits and the same $15,000 income cap.
  • Surviving spouse of a military member (SS): $126,526 off, and a full exemption for the spouse of a firefighter or peace officer killed in the line of duty.

Bring a Georgia driver's license showing your current address, the vehicle registration card showing Columbia County, a recorded deed, and income returns where the exemption has an income test. Any change to the deed, a refinance for example, requires a new application.

What does the January 1 rule mean if I sell my Columbia County house?

Georgia assigns a year's tax to whoever owned the property on January 1, and the county's tax office does not split the bill between buyer and seller. That split is a closing matter. The Columbus tax commissioner's explanation of the same state rule says a lien stays in the January 1 owner's name unless proof within 90 days of the due date shows the buyer contractually took the tax.

For you, that means two practical steps. First, read the proration line on the settlement statement and confirm the title company will pay the county, not leave it for the buyer to find. Second, if a Columbia County bill is still unpaid at closing, ask the Property Tax Division for the exact payoff for the closing date. The division mails each bill to the owner named in its records, so a seller who has moved should confirm the address on file.

The county's pay-tax page lets you view the tax on a parcel online, which helps you spot a balance before a buyer's title search does.

How are delinquent Columbia County taxes enforced?

The county first tries a letter or phone call, and if that fails it uses a levy and a sheriff's tax sale. The delinquent tax page says most matters are settled without a sale, and that the county has one of the highest collection rates in Georgia.

Sheriff's tax sales are public auctions that open at the amount of tax owed, and they are held on the first Tuesday of the month when the office schedules one. The sale notice appears in the Augusta Chronicle legal ads about a month ahead, as well as on the county site.

An owner who is behind should talk to the division before the levy stage. Selling the house before a sale date is possible, because the payoff is settled from the proceeds at the closing table, but the numbers must be confirmed in writing first.

What other Columbia County rules touch a sale?

The county does not print a due date on the pages above, so read the date on your bill or ask the division. Georgia's usual window to contest a value is 45 days from the date of the assessment notice, and the notice itself states the deadline for your parcel.

More questions about Columbia County, GA Property Tax Guide

Where do I apply for a Columbia County homestead exemption?

At the Tax Commissioner's Property Tax Division in Evans, 630 Ronald Reagan Drive, Building C, Second Floor. Applications are accepted year-round, but the county says the benefit for the current year requires filing by April 1.

Do I need to reapply after refinancing?

Yes. The county states that any change to a deed, a refinance for example, requires a new homestead application.

Is there a Columbia County exemption with no income limit?

Yes. The local school exemption for homeowners 70 or older covers the school tax on the house and up to three contiguous acres, and the county describes it as having no income limit.

How often are Columbia County tax sales held?

On the first Tuesday of the month, when the office schedules one. They are sheriff's tax sales run as auctions, and the notice is published in the Augusta Chronicle about a month earlier.

Can I pay Columbia County property tax online?

Yes, through the county's pay-tax page. A credit card carries a third-party fee, an eCheck carries $1.50 per item, and the county asks escrow customers to check with their lender first.

Coweta County by the numbers

Where do Coweta County owners take property tax questions?

Newnan holds both offices owners need. The Tax Commissioner at 87 Newnan Station Drive, Suite 100, handles bills and payments, and its number is 770-254-2670. The Assessor's Office at 37 Perry Street decides values and homestead claims, and its number is 770-254-2680.

The commissioner's counter opens at 8am and closes at 4:30pm on weekdays. Two elected boards, the county commissioners and the school board, each set a millage rate, while a board named by the grand jury hears value disputes. A copy of your deed comes from the Clerk of Superior Court inside the Coweta County Justice Center, 72 Greenville Street, and the commissioner's FAQ lists 770-254-2690 for the clerk.

  • Value or exemption: Assessor's Office.
  • Bill, payoff or lien: Tax Commissioner.
  • Deed copy: Clerk of Superior Court.

What is Coweta County like for someone preparing to sell?

Coweta County lies in the Georgia Piedmont, southwest of Atlanta, and counts as Metro Atlanta. Newnan is the seat and biggest city. The state legislature drew the county lines on June 9, 1826, after the Creek cession, and the name honors the Koweta people.

Five cities share the map: Newnan, Senoia, Grantville, Palmetto and Chattahoochee Hills. Haralson, Moreland, Sharpsburg and Turin are towns. Palmetto and Chattahoochee Hills spill over into Fulton County. Local land history includes Shenandoah, a 7,400-acre planned town backed by a 1970 federal program, which was foreclosed on in 1981. Wikipedia places the eastern half of the county in the Upper Flint River basin and the western half near Lake Harding on the Chattahoochee.

Population rose from 127,317 in 2010 to 146,158 in 2020, and QuickFacts shows 160,240 for July 2025. Census five-year estimates give owned homes a typical value of $357,500, with 78.4% of households owning. Rent averages $1,488 a month, household income is $95,548, and a commute takes 29.8 minutes on average.

What does the Coweta County tax calendar look like?

The commissioner's site says bills are mailed October 1 with payment due December 1. Mailing happens at least 60 days ahead. If the date on your printed bill differs, the printed date wins.

A drop box sits in the building's drive-through, and online card payments incur a fee that the card company collects. Checks sent by mail need a postmark by the due date. A closed office on the due date pushes payment to the next open day.

For general questions about Georgia property tax outside what the county answers, the commissioner's site points owners to the state Department of Revenue's local government services division at dor.georgia.gov.

  • January 1: ownership and use on this date fix the year's tax.
  • Through April 1: returns, first-year homestead filings and special program applications.
  • April 1: mobile and manufactured home tax, with a location decal issued after payment.
  • October 1: bills go in the mail.
  • December 1: due date for land, buildings and personal property.

What does Coweta County charge on late bills?

Interest builds monthly at prime plus three percentage points. A 5% penalty first applies at day 120, adds again every 120 days, and stops at 20%. A homesteaded bill below $500 escapes the penalty.

After about a month of non-payment, the commissioner may file a FiFa lien with the superior court clerk, on the General Execution Docket. The site says the lien stays on a credit record for seven years at minimum. Delinquent notices go out only now and then, so the office tells owners to ask for the current balance before sending money.

Mobile and manufactured homes carry a different risk: a missed April 1 payment and permit brings a 10% penalty, a citation to Coweta County State Court, or possible sale of the home.

Who pays the Coweta County tax when a house changes hands?

The January 1 owner is the name on the lien. A seller who receives a bill after the sale should hand it to the buyer, but the lien moves only if the commissioner gets proof of a contract or closing statement by day 90 after the due date.

So a seller whose closing prorated the tax should carry the settlement statement to Newnan Station Drive. Once the office has it, a bill that stays unpaid leads to a lien against the new owner.

Timing matters. Bills are mailed in October, so a spring or summer closing usually happens before that year's bill exists and the title company must estimate. Ask the commissioner for last year's total as a benchmark, and ask the closer how the estimate was set.

A buyer reading a Coweta County listing should also know that the bill covers the whole tax year, not just the months after the sale. When that matters in a negotiation, put the tax split in the contract in plain words so both sides and the closer work from the same page.

What are the three ways to appeal in Coweta County?

You have 45 days from the assessment notice. The first move is a written appeal on the state's uniform form, filed with the Board of Assessors, and it must name the route you want. Taxability, value, uniformity and a denied exemption are all valid grounds.

Appeal routes the Coweta County Tax Commissioner describes
RouteBest suited toWhat follows
Equalization boardMost homeownersHearing, then Superior Court if needed
Hearing officerNon-homestead real property valued at $1,000,000 or moreDecision, then Superior Court if needed
ArbitrationOwners holding a current certified appraisalHearing within 30 days; the ruling is final

Under the equalization route, the assessors can revise the value and mail a new notice, which you may appeal within 30 days. An appeal they leave unchanged moves forward on its own to a hearing. For arbitration, the assessors must acknowledge the appeal within 45 days, and if they reject your appraisal they must certify the case to the Clerk of Superior Court.

Which exemptions and special programs apply in Coweta County?

To claim a homestead you must have owned the house and lived in it on January 1, and the application has to arrive by April 1 of the first year. A late filing takes effect a year later. The assessors rule on every claim, a denial can be appealed, and you may not claim a homestead on any other property.

Coweta County also has local exemptions that replace the state figure whenever they are larger. The assessors will tell you what proof they want for age, income or military service. After approval the exemption renews without a new application until you move or the owner changes.

  • Deferral: for owners 62 and over with gross household income of $15,000 or less, tax waits until the ownership changes or the balance plus interest reaches 85% of fair market value.
  • Agricultural use: qualifying farmland is assessed at 30% of fair market value.
  • Conservation Use and Forest Land Protection: covenants of 10 or 15 years.
  • Historic property and Hazardous Site Reuse: preferential assessment, each applied for in the first four months of the year it starts.

A buyer of an enrolled tract should ask the assessors whether the covenant carries over.

More questions about Coweta County, GA Property Tax Guide

Which office in Coweta County sends my property tax bill?

The Tax Commissioner, at 87 Newnan Station Drive, Suite 100, Newnan. Bills go out October 1, and you can call 770-254-2670.

Is December 1 the Coweta County due date for every bill?

For land, buildings and personal property, yes, per the commissioner's site. Mobile and manufactured homes are due April 1, and the printed bill states the date that applies to you.

Can a hearing officer decide my Coweta County homestead appeal?

No. The county limits hearing officers to disputes over the value of non-homestead real property worth $1,000,000 or more.

Where do I get my deed in Coweta County?

From the Clerk of Superior Court at the Coweta County Justice Center, 72 Greenville Street, Newnan, GA 30263. The commissioner's FAQ gives 770-254-2690 for the clerk.

Do Coweta County penalties apply to every unpaid bill?

Not to homesteaded property with a bill under $500. Other unpaid bills take the 5% penalty after 120 days, repeating every 120 days up to a 20% cap.

Which desk bills and collects property tax in Crawford County?

Crawford County divides the work between two offices. One mails and collects the bills, and the other decides what each parcel is worth. Sellers end up calling both.

What should a seller know about Crawford County land and roads?

Crawford County lies in west central Georgia and is counted in the Macon metropolitan area. Knoxville holds the courthouse, and Roberta is the biggest town. With about 325 square miles of land and roughly 37 people per square mile, most parcels are rural.

The eastern fall line cuts the county roughly in half, which leaves the north hillier and the south flatter, with more cropland. Interstate 75, U.S. 80, U.S. 341 and State Routes 42, 96 and 128 cross the county, and the Fall Line Freeway touches a small part of the south along State Route 96. Monroe, Bibb, Peach, Taylor, Macon and Upson counties border it, and Houston County meets its far eastern edge. When is Crawford County property tax due?

The county site gives December 20 as the usual due date for real estate. Bills normally go out in mid-October, addressed to the person who held title at the start of the year.

The Department of Revenue's county sheet adds that a county may move that date to December 1 or November 15, or split billing into installments, and that interest waits until 60 days after the bill's postmark. Read the date printed on your own bill before scheduling a closing.

  • Interest on late tax runs at the bank prime loan rate plus 3 percent, accrued monthly. The rate is reset each calendar year from the first weekly Federal Reserve posting.
  • An added 5 percent penalty applies at each 120-day mark after the due date.
  • FiFa charges are added once the bill goes on the General Execution Docket.
  • Mobile homes taxed off-digest are due May 1, then draw a 10 percent penalty and 1 percent interest a month.

Lenders do not get bills from this office, according to the county. Owners with escrow should check that the servicer has the figures, and anyone whose mailed copy never showed up can request a duplicate.

How does Crawford County set the amount of tax?

The tax equals 40 percent of the assessors' fair market value times the millage rate, using the parcel's worth on January 1. County commissioners set one rate, the school board sets another, and Crawford County adds its garbage fee to the same statement.

A rollback rate is the rate that would collect last year's revenue after values rise. Going above it means three public hearings. The 2023 notice from Crawford County announced a levy 26.5 percent over rollback, with hearings on August 1, 15 and 29 at the courthouse at 100 GA Hwy 42 S in Knoxville. A 2021 notice shows the county also publishes its tax digest and five-year levy history in its news section.

Ask the tax commissioner for the millage on your parcel. An old bill is a poor guide, because both boards can change their rates every year.

What is the process to contest a Crawford County valuation?

Send a written appeal to the Tax Assessors. The tax commissioner's office will not take it. The clock is 45 days, counted from the day the assessment notice was mailed, and the county says notices generally arrive in spring.

A return filed in the first three months of the year lets you state your own value and sets up the notice. Owners are not required to file every year. Because the state sheet says the appeal must carry a postmark inside the window, a mailing receipt is worth keeping.

If the Board of Assessors leaves the value unchanged, ask the assessors' office what the next level of appeal is and what deadline applies. A seller who gets a spring notice shortly before listing the house should read it closely, since the value feeds that year's bill and a buyer's expectations.

What exemptions can a Crawford County owner claim?

Homestead is the main one. Applications are taken all year, though April 1 closes the digest. The applicant must own the house, live in it on January 1, name Georgia as legal residence, and hold title personally. Service members must also name Georgia as home state.

  • Added relief begins at 62, and the applicant must have reached that age by January 1 of the filing year.
  • Disability claims need statements of total disability from two separate sources.
  • A veterans exemption is also offered through the assessors.
  • Agricultural, preferential, conservation use, historic and tax-exempt status all run through the same office.

Under the state sheet, skipping the application counts as waiving the exemption. An heir who takes over a house should ask the assessors about filing in the new owner's name instead of assuming the old one carries over.

How should unpaid Crawford County tax be handled before a sale?

Ask the tax commissioner for a written payoff before signing anything. The office tells people mailing overdue payments to phone first, because penalties and execution charges move the total.

The statement is addressed to the January 1 owner, so a seller closing in the fall is the named taxpayer for that year. Put the split in the sale contract and ask the closing agent to carry the payoff into the settlement numbers.

Mobile homes add a step. All taxes must be paid and a current decal displayed before one is moved out of the county.

More questions about Crawford County, GA Property Tax Guide

Where do I pay Crawford County property tax?

In person at 640 GA Hwy 128, Suite 134, in Roberta, or through the mail to P.O. Box 634 at the same town. The office takes checks, cash, money orders and credit or debit cards, and the county site links to online payment.

Does Crawford County mail my tax bill to my mortgage company?

No. The county states that it does not bill lenders. If you pay through escrow, make sure the servicer has the amount, and phone (478) 836-3575 for a duplicate if yours never arrived.

Who do I contact to change the owner name on a Crawford County parcel?

The Tax Assessors, at (478) 836-2800. Notices go to the last known address of the January 1 owner, and the commissioner's desk does not process these updates.

Can I still file for homestead in Crawford County after April 1?

You can still turn in the form, but it will not reach that year's digest, because April 1 is the cutoff.

Is there any way around a missed Crawford County appeal deadline?

The state's county fact sheet says the appeal must be postmarked within 45 days of the notice's mailing date, so a late one risks being turned away. Keep the notice, note the mailing date, and send your written appeal to the Tax Assessors well before the last day.

Which Crisp County offices deal with a property tax bill?

In Crisp County two separate offices share the work. One office collects county and school tax. The other, run by the appraisal staff in Cordele, sets values. Elected county commissioners then adopt the millage rates that turn a value into a bill.

State revenue officials list crispcountytax.com as the collector's web address and crispcounty.com for the appraisers and commissioners. The county's administrative building is at 210 S. 7th Street in Cordele, and the appraisal staff answer at (229) 276-2635. For the commissioner's counter hours, payment options and your exact balance, ask the Crisp County tax commissioner directly.

County commissioners meet in Room 305 of the Government Center every second Tuesday morning, at nine. The county says that board adopts the budget and sets the property tax rate, so that meeting is where a rate debate plays out.

What is Crisp County, GA, and why does its geography matter to sellers?

Crisp County covers 281 square miles in south central Georgia, of which 8.4 are water. Cordele is both the courthouse town and the lone city. Arabi is a town, Wenona a census-designated place and Coney an unincorporated community. The whole county makes up the Cordele micropolitan area.

Two river systems share the land. The western two thirds drains to the middle Flint River, and the eastern third belongs to the Alapaha River basin of the Suwannee. Interstate 75 crosses it, as do U.S. 41, U.S. 280 and State Routes 33, 90, 257 and 300. Lawmakers carved the county out of Dooly in August 1905.

Neighbors are Dooly to the north, Wilcox to the east, Turner to the southeast, Worth to the southwest, and Lee and Sumter to the west. A county water notice also mentions the Lake Blackshear area water system, which serves customers across Crisp, Sumter and Worth counties, which is a detail for sellers near the water to confirm with the utility.

What do the latest Census estimates say about Crisp County homes?

Crisp County lost more residents than any of the four counties in this QuickFacts comparison. Census takers counted 23,439 people in 2010 and 20,128 in 2020. The newest estimate, 19,237, means a further slide of 4.4 percent.

  • Housing units, July 2025: 9,989 against 7,908 households.
  • Owner-occupied share: 55.5 percent, the smallest of any county in the comparison.
  • Value of the typical owned home in the 2020 to 2024 survey: $140,200.
  • Rent for the typical rental unit: $778 per month.
  • Share of residents in poverty: 22.8 percent.
  • Household income at the midpoint: $45,105.
  • Permits for new housing in 2025: 27.

The numbers describe a market with lower home values than any of its three comparison counties and few new permits. Rents run lower than elsewhere in the set, a point for anyone weighing whether to keep the house as a rental.

What jobs and commutes shape Crisp County housing demand?

Crisp County residents drive an average of 20.6 minutes to work, the shortest trip among the four counties in the same QuickFacts comparison. The county reports 503 employer establishments employing 7,557 people in 2023, a 2.3 percent decline from 2022.

Health care and social assistance brought in about $168.5 million in 2022, the largest service line listed. Retail sales that year were about $570 million, which works out to $28,902 per resident. Transportation and warehousing receipts were about $48.3 million.

Short drives and a base of health care and retail jobs mean many buyers will be local households. The county Assessors can show recent sales on your street.

What dates control a Crisp County property tax year?

Georgia's county fact sheet for Crisp County sets the rhythm of the year. The table gathers each rule it states.

Crisp County property tax calendar and rules (source: Georgia Department of Revenue county fact sheet)
ItemRule on the fact sheet
Returns of propertyJanuary 1 through April 1, filed with the county tax office
Homestead applicationAny time, up to April 1 of the first year of the exemption

Interest grace60 days from the postmark of the bill

Refund claimWithin three years of payment
Mobile home permitWithin 30 days of placement, then January 1 to April 1 yearly

A county can pick an earlier date, so the one on your bill governs. Phone the tax commissioner to confirm it before fixing a closing day.

How do I question a Crisp County assessment?

Start with the assessment notice. Your challenge goes to the Board of Tax Assessors rather than the collector, and the state sheet requires a postmark no more than 45 days after the notice was sent.

The Assessors' office publishes a standing notice that appraisal staff may visit parcels during the digest year to measure structures, list construction details and photograph the property. If an appraiser visits, ask what changed in the record. Tell the office about repairs, water damage or an unfinished room that lowers value, since the record is built from what the county has on file.

  • Last day to file a return describing your own view of value: April 1.
  • Questions about a review notice: (229) 276-2635.
  • Put the appeal on paper and keep a postmarked copy.
  • A claim for tax paid in error has to begin within three years of the payment.

How does the Crisp County millage process work?

Rates in Crisp County are adopted by the Board of Commissioners for county tax and by the school board for school tax. When a county plans to collect more than the rollback rate, Georgia requires public hearings. The Crisp County public notices page lists the 2026 current tax digest along with a five-year history of levy.

That page also carries hearing letters for zoning matters and election notices. A seller who plans to list should compare the five-year levy history with the bill on the house, because buyers will ask what the yearly tax runs.

The county site does not give a bill amount for any parcel. Ask the Assessors for the value on file and the tax commissioner for the millage that applies.

What if the seller of a Crisp County house still owes tax?

Get a payoff statement from the tax commissioner and have the settlement agent pay it out of the sale proceeds. Clearing the balance at closing keeps the county bill from following the house to the buyer.

  • Cities levy their own tax and the state sheet says the city clerk bills it, so a house inside Cordele or Arabi may carry a second bill. Ask whether either city's tax is collected with the county's.
  • A mobile home needs a location permit within 30 days of being set in place, renewed each winter before April 1.
  • A buyer's lender has 90 days to record a long-term security instrument, with intangible tax of $1.50 per $500 of the note, usually collected by the superior court clerk.

An heir selling an inherited Crisp County house should gather the last bill, confirm whether a homestead exemption was on file, and ask the Assessors whether a new application is needed in the heir's name.

More questions about Crisp County, GA Property Tax Guide

Which office takes Crisp County property tax payments?

The tax commissioner, whose website the state lists as crispcountytax.com. Ask that office for counter hours, payment methods and your balance.

What is the deadline to appeal a Crisp County valuation?

Forty-five days after the assessment notice is mailed. Send it to the Board of Tax Assessors with a postmark inside that window.

How long is the interest-free window after a Crisp County bill is mailed?

Georgia gives 60 days from the postmark on the bill before interest starts, although late balances can still pick up penalties. The official due date is December 20 unless the county has chosen an earlier one.

Is Crisp County growing or shrinking?

Shrinking. Counts fell from 23,439 in 2010 to 20,128 in 2020, and the July 2025 estimate sits at 19,237.

What is the typical home price in Crisp County?

Federal survey data for 2020 to 2024 shows $140,200 as the value of the typical owner-occupied house. Individual sales can land above or below it.
