Which Dawson County offices handle my property tax?

Dawson County runs property tax through two departments in the same building. The Tax Assessor sets values and receives exemption forms. The Tax Commissioner bills, collects and disburses all taxes under Georgia law, and also acts as the state's motor vehicle tag and title agent.

The commissioner is at 25 Justice Way, Suite 1222, inside the courthouse in downtown Dawsonville, reachable at (706) 344-3520 on weekdays between eight and five. The office runs its own site at dawsoncountytax.com and takes property tax payments by phone at (706) 701-2576. The assessor is down the hall at Suite 1201, on (706) 344-3590, and keeps a separate website with a property search, a sales search and a tax estimator.

Ask the Dawson County tax commissioner for the due date that applies to your parcel.

What does the Dawson County landscape mean for a house sale?

Dawson County sits in the Blue Ridge foothills and counts as part of metro Atlanta. Dawsonville holds the courthouse and is the only city. Juno and Afton are unincorporated. The land covers about 211 square miles, with ridges along the northern and western edges that reach roughly 3,500 feet.

Part of Lake Lanier lies in the southeast corner, and the Chestatee and Etowah rivers cross the county. Amicalola Falls, which drops 729 feet, is the tallest cascading waterfall east of the Mississippi and one of Georgia's Seven Natural Wonders. Black Mountain, at 3,600 feet, is the highest point. Fannin, Lumpkin, Hall, Forsyth, Cherokee, Pickens and Gilmer counties surround it, and part of the Chattahoochee National Forest falls inside the county line.

Lawmakers formed the county in December 1857 from parts of Gilmer and Lumpkin. It later became known for stock car racing, tied to moonshine runs on State Route 9, called Thunder Road, and a festival celebrates that history each October. Lake and mountain views, forest edges and slopes all change how a house is valued, so read your assessment notice with those features in mind.

How fast is Dawson County growing and what do houses cost?

Dawson County is the fastest-growing of the four Georgia counties in the Census Bureau's side-by-side QuickFacts table. The 2020 count of 26,798 rose to an estimated 35,365 by July 2025, an increase of 32.0 percent from the 2020 base.

  • Value of the typical owned home in the 2020 to 2024 survey: $406,700, over double any other county in the table.
  • Typical monthly rent: $1,626.
  • Housing units: 14,876, and 11,573 households.
  • Share of homes lived in by owners: 78.7 percent.
  • Households earning at the midpoint: $92,991 a year.
  • Building permits in 2025: 1,069, against 135 in Decatur County.
  • Residents 25 and older holding a four-year degree: 36.4 percent.

With values like these, the 40 percent assessment on a Dawson County house is a large base. A seller can use the tax estimator on the assessor's site to answer buyers' questions about yearly tax from the county's own tool.

Which special assessment programs does Dawson County offer?

Dawson County's assessor describes several programs that reduce the value taxed. Most need a 10-year covenant and an application between January 1 and April 1.

Dawson County special assessment programs (source: Dawson County Tax Assessor FAQ)
ProgramWhat the county says
Preferential agriculturalBona fide farm property assessed at 30 percent of fair market value instead of 40 percent, 10-year commitment
Conservation useAssessed at current use value, 10-year commitment, savings that can top 50 percent in some cases
Environmentally sensitiveCurrent use value for land kept natural and meeting Department of Natural Resources rules, 10 years
Residential transitionalCurrent use value for homes in areas shifting to other uses, 10-year covenant
TimberStanding timber untaxed until sold or harvested, then taxed at 100 percent of value
Equipment and fixturesAssessed at 40 percent of fair market value

Anyone selling acreage under one of these covenants should ask the assessor what happens to the covenant when ownership changes, because the county says the commitment runs for ten years.

When must Dawson County exemptions and returns be filed?

April 1 is the date that matters. Real property returns, personal property returns, conservation use and forest land applications, requests for parcel splits or combinations, and exemptions are all taken from January 1 through April 1. The assessor says no extension has been given for any type of exemption.

  • Regular homestead applications can be accepted year-round, but they must be in by April 1 to count for that tax year.
  • Senior and other specialized exemptions follow the same April 1 deadline.
  • Exemption applications are taken in person only.
  • After you receive an exemption, you do not reapply unless you move to another address.

Dawson County also publishes a list of assessment notices that came back undeliverable, as Georgia's O.C.G.A. 48-5-306(c) directs. If you changed addresses or inherited a parcel, check that list on the assessor's website so a missed notice does not cost you the appeal window.

How do I challenge a Dawson County valuation?

Appeals must be written and arrive within 45 days of the assessment notice. The county calls late ones invalid. Grounds are limited to taxability, uniformity with similar properties and value.

The assessors look at it first. When they leave the value alone, a three-person Board of Equalization named by the Grand Jury hears it. A taxpayer or the assessor who disagrees may then go to Superior Court.

Appeal volume has been unusually heavy. Under O.C.G.A. 48-5-311, a county where appeals reach 3 percent of parcels, or 3 percent of the digest's value, gets an extra 180 days to decide them. The assessor's page states that Dawson County crossed that threshold on June 7, 2024. Field appraisers handling appeals and reviews carry photo identification and drive marked county vehicles, and the county asks owners with questions to call (706) 344-3590.

How is the tax calculated in Dawson County?

The assessor's FAQ explains that the levy applies to 40 percent of fair market value, fixed at the start of each year. Millage is set annually. The county defines a mill as a dollar of tax for each $1,000 of assessed value. Property tax pays for police and fire services, schools, roads, bridges, water and parks, according to the county.

Fair market value means the amount a knowledgeable buyer would pay and a willing seller would accept in an arm's-length sale. The assessors use cost, market and income approaches. The market approach compares sales of similar properties, which is why a run of high-priced sales on your road tends to push your value up.

Ask the Dawson County tax commissioner for the millage that applies to your address, and use the assessor's estimator to test a number before you compare it with the bill.

What should a Dawson County seller do about the tax bill?

Request the balance from the tax commissioner before the sale contract is final. The county's FAQ says tax is charged to the owner on January 1, so a seller who closes later in the year may hold that year's bill. Write the split into the contract.

  • Mobile home bills carry their own date. The commissioner's site shows the 2026 mobile home bills were due April 1.
  • Payment options include the counter at Suite 1222 and the pay-by-phone line, (706) 701-2576.
  • If the house is under a conservation or agricultural covenant, tell the buyer and the assessor.
  • If an estate is selling, ask the assessor what documents are needed to update the owner and the homestead record.

Whoever the buyer is, obtain the payoff in writing and route it through the settlement agent.

More questions about Dawson County, GA Property Tax Guide

Where is the Dawson County tax commissioner's office?

At 25 Justice Way, Suite 1222, inside the courthouse in downtown Dawsonville. Staff answer weekdays from eight to five at (706) 344-3520.

Can I pay my Dawson County property tax by phone?

Yes. The commissioner's website lists (706) 701-2576 for paying property tax by phone. You can also call the main office at (706) 344-3520 or pay at the counter.

What is the filing deadline for a Dawson County homestead exemption?

April 1. Regular homestead applications can be taken year-round, but one that arrives after April 1 does not count for that tax year, and applications must be made in person.

What is the Dawson County appeal period?

Forty-five days after the assessment notice arrives, and the appeal must be written. Late filings are invalid, per the county.

Is Dawson County property expensive compared with nearby Georgia counties?

Yes. The survey value for a typical owned home is $406,700 here, against $164,100 in Crawford, $140,200 in Crisp and $158,800 in Decatur.

Which Bainbridge desks handle Decatur County property tax?

Two courthouse offices in Bainbridge split the job. One office prepares the digest, mails the bills and takes payment. The other, the assessors, puts a value on every real and personal parcel. Both operate inside the courthouse on West Water Street.

Collection happens on the ground floor of the courthouse, 112 W. Water St., Monday to Friday between 8 and 5. Call (229) 248-3021 about property tax, (229) 248-3019 for motor vehicles or (229) 248-3009 for the tag office. Letters go to P.O. Box 246, Bainbridge, and decaturcountytax.com is the office's website. Valuation questions go to (229) 248-3008 or to P.O. Box 1106 in the same city.

Roughly 20,000 property tax bills and 3,300 mobile home bills go out each year, according to the collector's site. What comes in is sent on to the state, county, schools, library and cities every other week.

How does the geography of Decatur County affect a sale?

Decatur County is the largest of the four Georgia counties in the Census comparison, with 623 square miles, of which about 597 are land. It reaches the Florida line on its southern edge, and Bainbridge holds the courthouse. The county makes up the Bainbridge micropolitan area, one piece of the Tallahassee and Bainbridge combined statistical area.

Most of the county drains to the lower Flint River around Bainbridge. The southwestern corner near Attapulgus drains toward the Ochlockonee, and a sliver in the far southwest reaches the Apalachicola. U.S. 27, U.S. 84 and State Routes 97, 241, 253, 262, 285, 302, 309, 310 and 311 carry traffic. Miller, Mitchell, Baker, Grady and Seminole counties border it, and Gadsden County, Florida, lies to the south.

Attapulgus, Bainbridge and Climax are cities, Brinson is a town, and Faceville is a census-designated place. Amsterdam, Ausmac and Cyrene are unincorporated communities. The county dates to December 8, 1823, when it was split from Early County, and it later gave up land to Thomas, Grady and Seminole counties. Because several cities lie inside the county, check whether your parcel also owes a city bill.

What do the newest Census figures say about Decatur County housing?

Headcount here has been flat lately. Census figures were 27,842 in 2010 and 29,367 in 2020, and the 2025 estimate of 29,432 compares with a revised 2020 base of 29,479.

  • Housing units: 13,601, with 10,621 households.
  • Owner-occupied share: 62.1 percent.
  • Value of the typical owned home, 2020 to 2024: $158,800.
  • Typical rent: $838 monthly.
  • Income for the midpoint household: $53,317, with 21.7 percent of residents in poverty.
  • Housing permits in 2025: 135.
  • Mean commute: 21.4 minutes.

The county has 626 employer establishments and 7,687 employees as of 2023, up 2.8 percent from the year before. Its transportation and warehousing receipts of about $60.6 million in 2022 were the highest of the four counties compared. Retail sales were about $451 million, or $15,551 per resident, well below the figure for Crisp or Dawson County.

What are the key tax dates in Decatur County?

Decatur County sets December 20 as the yearly deadline for property tax and April 1 for mobile homes. Both dates are on the county's commissioner pages.

Decatur County tax dates and contacts (source: Decatur County tax commissioner and tax assessor pages)
ItemDetail
Real and personal property billsDue December 20
Mobile home billsDue April 1
Returns, conservation and agricultural applicationsJanuary 1 through April 1
Homestead applicationDuring the year, up to April 1 of the following year per the assessors' notice
Appeal of an assessment45 days from the mailing date printed on the notice
Board of Assessors meetingSecond Tuesday of each month, 8:30 a.m., Grand Jury Room

The state revenue department says a county can choose December 1 or November 15 instead, or bill in installments, and that interest holds off for 60 days after the bill is postmarked. Ask the commissioner what interest and penalties apply to a late bill.

How are appeals and exemption forms submitted in Decatur County?

Look at the top right corner of the assessment notice. The county prints the final appeal day there, 45 days after mailing, and it moves from year to year, so rely on your own paper.

The assessors' office also receives returns for real and personal property and applications for homestead, conservation use, preferential agricultural assessment, forest land conservation use assessment and Freeport. Blank forms sit on the Department of Revenue's forms page, and completed ones can go in by email, ordinary mail or the drop box outside the courthouse.

  • Returns and special-use applications: January 1 through April 1.
  • Homestead under Code Section 48-5-44: the application may be filed once the house is your primary residence, through April 1 of the next year.
  • Property records and parcel data: the county's qPublic site at qpublic.net/ga/decatur.
  • Board sessions: second Tuesday monthly, 8:30 in the morning, Grand Jury Room.

Will an appraiser visit my Decatur County property?

Possibly. A public notice from the assessors cites O.C.G.A. 48-5-264.1, which allows representatives with proper identification to enter property during normal business hours. Reasons include permits that were issued, a return of value, a revaluation of part or all of the county, parcel sales and appeal reviews.

The office says it uses building permits and other sources to update its records, and that appraisers visit where improvements were made or information looks wrong. If you added a room, finished a garage or tore something down, the permit trail may already have reached the assessors, so a seller should check what the record says before a buyer's agent does.

The assessors also assemble the tax digest, which is the compilation of property values, motor vehicle values, timber values and exemption amounts that goes to the State Revenue Commissioner. A change in your parcel's record flows into that report.

What if a Decatur County seller owes back tax or a mobile home bill?

Only the commissioner can quote a payoff. Phone (229) 248-3021, give the parcel number and your expected closing date, and ask for the number in writing.

  • A mobile home has its own April 1 bill, so check that account separately from any land.
  • Cities in the county levy their own tax, and the state says the city clerk bills it unless the city and county agreed to a single bill. Ask the commissioner whether yours is combined.
  • Refunds for tax wrongly collected must be requested within three years of the payment.
  • If the house passed through an estate, ask the assessors which documents they need to update the owner before the bill goes out.

Bills are charged to the owner on January 1 under Georgia's rules, so the sale contract should state who covers the portion of the year after closing. Have the settlement agent send the payoff directly to the commissioner and keep the receipt.

More questions about Decatur County, GA Property Tax Guide

Where do I pay Decatur County property tax in person?

At the courthouse, 112 W. Water St., Bainbridge, GA 39817, first floor. The counter runs weekdays 8 to 5, and the property tax number is (229) 248-3021.

What is the Decatur County payment deadline?

December 20, the commissioner's page says, with mobile homes due April 1. Confirm against your own bill, since a county may adopt another date.

How many days does a Decatur County owner have to appeal?

Forty-five days counted from the mailing date of the notice. The last filing day is printed in the notice's top right corner.

Does Decatur County have a drop box for tax forms?

Yes. The assessors list a drop box outside the courthouse, along with email and regular mail, as ways to submit forms and applications.

How large is Decatur County compared with its neighbors in Georgia?

Decatur County covers 623 square miles, with about 597 of them land. That is the largest of the four Georgia counties compared in the Census table, where Crawford, Crisp and Dawson cover roughly 325, 273 and 211 square miles of land.

Selling in DeKalb County? Get a Cash Offer

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Who to contact in DeKalb County

  • DeKalb County Tax Commissioner
  • DeKalb County Property Appraisal handles assessment and appeals.

What we confirmed on official pages

  • 5% penalty if installment not postmarked by due date; unpaid balances 120 days past deadline get 5% penalty every 120 days

What we could not confirm

  • Assessor page not fetched; URL unverified

Dekalb County by the numbers

Which DeKalb County offices value and bill property?

Two separate offices split the job. The Property Appraisal Department sets what your home is worth. The Tax Commissioner's Office then sends the bill and takes payment. The commissioner's office states plainly that it has no say over the assessed amount.

The DeKalb County Board of Commissioners adopts the millage rate each July. The Tax Commissioner's central property tax office is staffed weekdays from 8:00 a.m. until 5:00 p.m. at 404-298-4000. The Property Appraisal Department can be reached at 404-371-0841 about a value or a missing assessment notice.

Cities add their own levies. Atlanta, Brookhaven, Chamblee, Clarkston, Decatur, Doraville, Dunwoody, Lithonia, Pine Lake, Stone Mountain, Stonecrest and Tucker appear on the commissioner's exemption page with local rules, and Avondale does not award local exemptions.

What dates matter on a DeKalb County tax bill?

Bills go out in August, and the county's installment dates are September 30 and November 15. Paying in one lump sum means paying by September 30. If a deadline would be a Saturday or Sunday, the county pushes it to Monday, so the 2026 second installment landed on November 16.

The penalty for a late first or second installment is 5%, and a postmark after the date triggers it. Metered and kiosk postage dates are not accepted as proof, so near a deadline ask the post office to hand-cancel the envelope. Online payments must arrive by midnight on the deadline, Eastern time.

Balances still open 120 days after the deadline pick up a further 5% penalty, repeated every 120 days. Accounts with a balance after December 31 become subject to a lien.

Step in the tax yearTimingWho handles it
Assessment notice mailedMay; 45 days from the notice date to appealProperty Appraisal
Millage rate setJulyBoard of Commissioners
Homestead application onlineJanuary 1 to mid-JulyTax Commissioner
Bills mailedAugustTax Commissioner
Mailed payments windowAugust 15 to November 15Tax Commissioner
Installments dueSeptember 30 and November 15Tax Commissioner
Lien exposureBalances open after December 31Tax Commissioner

Table source: DeKalb County Tax Commissioner's Office, tax bill, payment and exemption pages.

What are the ways to pay a DeKalb tax bill?

Current-year payments can be mailed to DeKalb County Tax Commissioner, Property Tax Division, P.O. Box 117545, Atlanta, GA 30368-7545. Prior-year payments go to the Delinquent Collections Division, P.O. Box 100001, Decatur, GA 30031-7001. Checks must be in U.S. funds.

  • Phone: 678-501-7995, with no fee for an e-check
  • Online: the county's GovHub payment portal, searchable by parcel ID, address or owner name
  • Card: a 2.31% fee with a $1.50 minimum per transaction; international and commercial cards add 3.95%
  • A returned payment costs 5% of the check with a $30 minimum

Partial payments are accepted, and the first installment must be paid before the second. The portal handles real estate and business personal property accounts only; mobile home, public utility and heavy equipment accounts go by mail or to a county counter.

What is the route for contesting a DeKalb County assessment?

Read the May assessment notice and count 45 days from the date printed on it. Should the current-year value look wrong, the instructions for filing are included with the notice. State law lets the appeal rest on value, uniformity, taxability or a denied exemption, filed in writing with the board of assessors.

The Georgia Department of Revenue describes three tracks: the Board of Equalization, a hearing officer for non-homestead property valued above $500,000, or arbitration for value. A taxpayer still unhappy can file a notice of appeal for superior court inside 30 days of the decision, once taxes equal to the last year's amount are paid, as O.C.G.A. 48-5-29 requires.

An unresolved appeal does not stop the bill. DeKalb issues a temporary value, normally the lesser of the last final value or 85 percent of the current value. You can ask in your appeal to be billed at 100 percent instead. Interest applies to appeal differences settled after November 15, and the commissioner cites O.C.G.A. 48-5-311(e)(6) for the process.

What homestead exemptions can a DeKalb homeowner claim?

To claim the basic homestead exemption you must occupy the house as your main home on January 1 and hold title. It also asks for every vehicle registered at that address, a Georgia ID or license showing the property address, income taxes filed from the home, and no homestead claim anywhere else. Applications are not automatic, and neither a lender nor a closing attorney files one for you.

  • Special exemptions exist for owners 62 and older, disabled residents and disabled veterans, and several depend on income
  • An applicant must already hold a homestead exemption to add a special one
  • Applications are taken in person year-round and online from January 1 to mid-July
  • A county assessment freeze is available when you apply by April 1, and it does not cover school, city or state taxes

City programs differ. Brookhaven lists a $40,000 basic exemption, Chamblee $50,000, and Doraville $10,000 plus a 2.5 mill reduction. Clarkston gives homeowners 65 and older an extra $20,000. Decatur and Stone Mountain take applications at city hall rather than through the county.

Who owes the tax when a DeKalb County house sells mid-year?

Taxes follow the property, and the state sets the year-long liability at January 1. The state's FAQ puts the full year on whoever held the parcel on January 1, however soon after the sale closes. The January 1 owner of record gets the mailed bill, and a buyer whose deed is recorded afterward gets one too.

Who actually pays is a contract matter. The tax commissioner tells new owners to check with the closing attorney, mortgage company or escrow agent, or read the closing statement. Unpaid taxes keep accruing against the parcel, and DeKalb does not send bills to mortgage lenders, so an escrow account does not remove your duty to confirm payment.

Before listing, pull your parcel on the payment portal and confirm nothing is open. A parcel with a balance after December 31 can be liened, and the commissioner describes the lien, called a FiFa, as the first step toward a tax sale. Sales happen on the first Tuesday of a month in front of the DeKalb County Courthouse, and buyers pay with cash, a bank-issued cashier's check or a wire. Money left over after taxes and costs is held as excess funds until an entitled party claims it.

What do DeKalb County's Census numbers say about taxpayers?

QuickFacts shows 774,394 people in mid-2025, a 1.3% gain on the April 2020 estimate base. There are 287,239 households of 2.63 people on average, and seniors make up 15.1% of the population. Land area is 267.74 square miles with 2,854.9 people per square mile as of 2020.

Owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $1,979, those without one $715, and 12.7% of people live in poverty. Owners on fixed incomes should look at the senior and income-based exemptions on the commissioner's page.

More questions about DeKalb County, GA Property Tax Guide

When is the second DeKalb County property tax installment due?

November 15, shifted when it lands on a Saturday or Sunday. In 2026 it fell on a Sunday, so the date became November 16. A late payment carries a 5% penalty if the envelope is not postmarked by the due date.

Which office explains a DeKalb assessed value?

The Property Appraisal Department, at 404-371-0841. The Tax Commissioner's Office, at 404-298-4000, handles billing and has no authority over the value.

Can I pay my DeKalb tax bill in installments?

Yes. The county splits the bill into two installments, due September 30 and November 15, and the first must be paid before the second. Paying everything at once means paying by September 30.

Does the DeKalb homestead exemption apply automatically?

No. You must file an application, and a missed filing waives the exemption for that year under O.C.G.A. 48-5-45(a)(2). You can apply for the following year if you miss the cutoff.

What follows when DeKalb property taxes go unpaid?

Penalties and interest build, a lien can be filed after December 31, and the lien is the first step toward a tax sale. Pay the balance with fees and the lien is marked satisfied.

Where is Dodge County, Georgia, and which towns does it hold?

Dodge County lies in the southern part of Georgia, mostly in the Ocmulgee River watershed, and Eastman is both the seat of government and the biggest city. Wikipedia gives a total area of 503 square miles, of which the Census Bureau counts 495.96 as land.

The legislature organized the county on October 26, 1870, carving it mostly from Laurens County with smaller pieces of Pulaski, Montgomery and Telfair. The Macon and Brunswick Railroad had been built the year before, and towns grew up along the line far from the old county seat at Hawkinsville. Chauncey, Eastman and Milan are cities. Chester and Rhine are towns, and Empire is a census-designated place that crosses into Bleckley County.

Highways include US 23, US 280, US 341 and the US 319 and 441 corridor, plus State Routes 46 and 117 and several others. The Heart of Georgia Regional Airport lies three miles east of Eastman on State Route 46 and houses an aviation campus of Middle Georgia State College. A seller in Dodge County is usually dealing with a rural or small-town parcel, and the county's own offices handle nearly every step.

Who do Dodge County owners call about property tax?

On the county's services page, the Tax Commissioner is 478-374-2154 and the Tax Assessors are 478-374-8122. County government works out of 643 Pearl Bates Avenue in Eastman, and the clerk of courts answers at 478-374-2871.

State guidance divides the roles the same way statewide: the commissioner takes payments and, in most counties, homestead filings, while the assessors own the appraised value and appeal questions. The county website has a Tax Payments link for paying online. The cities and towns inside the county publish these numbers:

  • Chauncey: 229-868-2296
  • Chester: 478-358-4550
  • Eastman: 478-374-7721
  • Milan: 229-362-4290
  • Rhine: 229-385-5521

If your house sits inside a city, ask both the county and the city clerk whether city tax comes on a separate bill.

Has the 2026 assessment appeal window in Dodge County closed?

Dodge County mailed its 2026 tax assessment notices on June 19, 2026, and August 3, 2026 was the final day to appeal. For the 2026 digest that window is shut, so a seller who missed it lives with the 2026 value and watches for next year's notice.

The county announcement says appeals could be filed by email, by U.S. mail, or online through the appeal module on the qPublic site. Anyone who did not receive a notice, or who has a question about one, was told to call the assessors at 478-374-8122. The notice arrives every year, and the 45 days run from the day it was mailed, so mark the mailing date when it comes.

The county also raised the processing fee for conservation use (CUVA), forest land protection (FLPA) and other preferential parcels to $30.00 for new, renewal and continuation covenants, effective July 1, 2025. Owners of farm or timber land should ask the assessors whether a covenant is recorded on the parcel before listing.

What are my appeal options once I file in Dodge County?

The state's uniform appeal form makes you pick one of three tracks, and the completed form is sent to the Dodge County Board of Tax Assessors. State revenue staff have no power to override a local value.

TrackWhat it coversWhat happens next
Board of EqualizationValue, uniformity, taxability or a denied exemptionAssessors may revise the notice; if not, a hearing is scheduled and a decision follows
Hearing officerValue or uniformity of non-homestead real property worth more than $500,000Decision, then superior court if still disputed
ArbitrationValue onlyTaxpayer submits a certified appraisal within 45 days of the acknowledgment; hearing scheduled within 30 days

Table source: Georgia Department of Revenue, Filing a Property Tax Appeal.

  • Going to superior court takes a written notice to the assessors inside 30 days after the ruling
  • The board schedules a settlement conference after your appeal, with notice inside 45 days
  • The court will not hear the case until last year's amount of tax is paid
  • A final value at 85 percent or less of the earlier figure lets the taxpayer recover costs and attorney's fees

When are Dodge County property taxes due?

The state default is December 20, and a county may instead choose December 1, November 15 or installments. Interest also waits until 60 days after the bill was postmarked. Whatever date your Dodge bill prints controls, and the commissioner at 478-374-2154 can replace a lost bill.

Delinquent balances can pick up penalties on top of interest. Ask the tax commissioner what your parcel owes before a closing, request the figure in writing, and give a copy to whoever runs the closing.

A return of value can be filed from January 1 through April 1. An owner who paid last year and files nothing is treated as repeating last year's final value, so most homeowners never file one.

Does Dodge County offer homestead exemptions?

State revenue records show no local homestead exemptions in Dodge County beyond the statewide ones. An application can go in any time after the house becomes your primary residence, with April 1 as the cutoff for the first year of benefit.

Skipping the application forfeits that year's exemption. The standard state exemption takes $2,000 off assessed value, which is set at 40 percent of fair market value. The county's tax commissioner or assessors take the application, depending on how Dodge handles it, so ask which window applies.

Refunds exist for tax assessed or collected in error, with a claim due inside three years of payment. A seller does not get part of a year back, since ownership on January 1 fixes liability for the whole year.

What should a Dodge County seller know about taxes at closing?

The January 1 owner is liable for that year's bill, so a fall sale still carries a full year of tax. The sales contract decides how the year is split, and the closing statement shows who pays what.

Two recorded items matter at closing. A security deed on a long-term loan must be recorded in the county within 90 days, and an intangible tax applies to it, collected by the superior court clerk in most counties. A sale also triggers Georgia's transfer tax, which falls on the seller by law and is figured on the sale price at the clerk's office. A county tax lien is entered on the general execution docket at the clerk's office, which is where a title search finds it.

How big and how priced is the Dodge County housing stock?

QuickFacts lists 19,663 residents for 2025, a 1.7% drop since April 2020, along with 8,643 housing units and just 5 building permits for the year.

  • Share of homes lived in by their owners: 70.6%
  • Middle home value: $118,100
  • Median gross rent: $723
  • Median household income: $51,587
  • Residents 65 and older: 20.8%
  • People per square mile (2020): 40.2

For comparison, the same table gives $357,800 for DeKalb County, so a Dodge County house sits at a much lower price point. Check the parcel's tax status before you list, since a back-tax balance weighs more against a lower sale price.

More questions about Dodge County, GA Property Tax Guide

Which number reaches Dodge County's tax office?

Call the Dodge County Tax Commissioner at 478-374-2154. The Tax Assessors, at 478-374-8122, answer questions about values and appeals.

Can I still appeal my 2026 Dodge County assessment?

For the 2026 digest, yes. Notices were mailed June 19, 2026, and August 3 was the final day was August 3, 2026. Watch for the next annual notice and count 45 days from its mailing date.

Does Dodge County have its own homestead exemption?

No. State records list none beyond the statewide exemption, which owners request through the county tax office by April 1 of the first benefit year.

When are Dodge County property taxes due?

The state default is December 20 unless the county sets another date or installments. Owners also get 60 days from the bill's postmark before interest. Use the date printed on your bill.

Can I get property tax back after selling my Dodge County house?

Georgia law does not refund a partial year, because the January 1 owner is liable for all of it. A refund is available only for tax assessed or collected in error, with a claim within three years of payment.

What kind of county is Dooly County, Georgia?

Dooly County is a rural county in central Georgia with Vienna as its seat. The legislature created it on May 15, 1821, from land ceded by the Creek Nation, and named it for Colonel John Dooly, a Revolutionary War fighter. Crisp County was cut out of its original borders, along with parts of Macon, Pulaski, Turner, Wilcox and Worth counties, so its original borders covered far more ground than the present county.

Wikipedia reports 397 square miles in the upper Atlantic coastal plain. Most of the western two-thirds drains to the Flint River, the northeast and east drain to the Ocmulgee, and the far southeast corner reaches the Alapaha basin. Neighbors are Houston, Pulaski, Wilcox, Crisp, Sumter and Macon counties.

Lilly, Byromville, Pinehurst, Unadilla and Vienna are the cities, and Dooling, Drayton and Findlay are towns. Unadilla is the largest. The 2020 census counted no urban residents at all, so nearly every sale here is a farm, small-town or acreage property, and the county offices in Vienna handle most steps.

Where are the Dooly County tax offices and what are their hours?

Three county offices matter to a seller, and the first two share a building at 105 W. Cotton Street in Vienna.

OfficeLocationPhoneHours
Tax Commissioner105 W. Cotton Street, Room 1; mailing address P.O. Box 371229-268-4212Mon to Thu, 7:30 a.m. to 6 p.m.; closed Fri
Assessors Office105 W. Cotton Street, Room 2229-268-4719Weekdays, 8 to noon and 1 to 5
Commissioners' Office113 N. Third Street, Room 1229-268-4228Call for hours

Table source: Dooly County, Georgia, official website.

The tax commissioner's page also links an online payment portal and a tag renewal link to the Georgia DRIVES site. Because the commissioner's office closes on Fridays, plan any payoff request or in-person payment for Monday through Thursday.

Did Dooly County raise its millage rate for 2025?

The county posted a notice that its commissioners had tentatively adopted a 2025 millage rate requiring a 2.62% increase in property tax revenue. The proposed rate was 17.45 mills, up 0.445 mills, against a no-increase rate of 17.005 mills.

Three public hearings were set at the commissioners' office on 113 N. Third Street: two on Thursday, September 4, at 10:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m., and one on Friday, September 19, at 10:00 a.m. Those hearing dates have passed, so a seller should ask the tax commissioner for the final rate that appears on the current bill. The notice itself worked out two sample increases, about $25.81 for a homestead with a fair market value of $150,000 and about $26.70 for a non-homestead property of the same value.

Georgia sets assessed value at 40 percent of fair market value, and the millage rate applies to that assessed figure. The notice covers the county's own levy; ask the tax commissioner which school and city rates appear on a given parcel's bill.

How does a Dooly County owner contest a value?

Begin by phoning the Assessors Office at 229-268-4719. Each year the board mails a notice of assessment, and an owner who rejects the stated fair market value gets 45 days, counted from the mailing date, to file. The postmark has to fall inside that window.

  • Reasons include taxability, value, uniformity and a refused exemption
  • On the state's PT-311A form you choose among equalization board, hearing officer and arbitration
  • Email is allowed only if the board has a written policy accepting electronic service
  • The state revenue department does not receive the form

The notice itself carries the filing instructions, so keep the envelope or note the postmark date. A refund for tax that was erroneously or illegally collected must be requested in writing within three years of payment.

What returns and exemptions apply to Dooly County property?

The county tax office takes returns of value in the first quarter, January 1 to April 1. Silence counts as a repeat of last year's value for anyone who paid then. For homestead, apply once the house is your primary residence and before April 1 of the first benefit year; a missed application forfeits that year.

The Department of Revenue's Dooly page describes the state exemptions without a local add-on, so ask the commissioner whether the county offers anything beyond them. The commissioner's page links a tax information pamphlet with homestead details. Ask the office for a current copy before you rely on older figures.

Voters can also exempt commercial and industrial inventory under the freeport exemption, which is requested from the board of assessors during the return period. That rule affects owners of a shop or warehouse building, not a typical house.

What do mobile home and vehicle rules mean for a Dooly County sale?

Mobile homes follow their own track. State rules call for a location permit from the tax commissioner within 30 days of placement, renewed every year in the first quarter. A mobile home sitting in the county on January 1 is returned for taxation by April 1, together with the permit.

  • A mobile home on land you are selling needs its permit and return current
  • Vehicle registration renews with the commissioner in the 30 days ending on the owner's birthday
  • A newly bought vehicle needs registration within 30 days
  • Only the tax commissioner can collect motor vehicle tax

Ask the tax commissioner to confirm the status of any mobile home on the parcel before a buyer's lender does.

What taxes come due when a Dooly County house sells?

Whoever holds title on January 1 carries that whole year's ad valorem tax, even after a spring or summer sale. How the bill is divided is a contract term, and the closing statement should show the proration.

At recording, the seller owes Georgia's real estate transfer tax. The revenue department publishes the schedule and the closing agent calculates it. A long-term note secured by land also triggers an intangible recording tax, with the security instrument recorded locally inside 90 days. Tax liens, whether county or state, are entered on the clerk's general execution docket.

The usual state due date is December 20 unless the county picks another, and interest waits 60 days after the bill is postmarked. Request a payoff figure from the commissioner for your closing agent.

What does the Census say about Dooly County homes?

The 2025 estimate is 11,156 people, off 0.5% since April 2020, living among 4,906 housing units. Builders pulled only 22 permits in 2025.

  • Owner-occupied share, 2020 to 2024: 64.7%
  • Typical owned-home value: $107,400
  • Median gross rent: $758
  • Median household income: $60,987
  • Residents living in poverty: 25.6%
  • Residents 65 and older: 22.1%
  • Households with broadband: 76.6%

Wikipedia's reading of the 2020 census shows 4,762 housing units with 15.0% vacant, and county population fell from 14,918 in 2010 to 11,208 in 2020.

More questions about Dooly County, GA Property Tax Guide

When is the Dooly County tax office open?

Monday through Thursday from 7:30 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., and closed Friday. Find it at 105 W. Cotton Street, Room 1, Vienna, or call 229-268-4212.

What is the deadline to dispute a Dooly County value?

Forty-five days after the notice went in the mail. File in writing with the county board of tax assessors rather than the state, and call 229-268-4719 with questions.

Does Dooly County have a homestead exemption?

The state exemption is available, and the revenue department's Dooly page describes no local add-on, so ask the commissioner about anything more. Apply by April 1 of the first year you want it, since a missed application waives that year.

What was Dooly County's proposed 2025 millage rate?

The county's notice proposed 17.45 mills, an increase of 0.445 mills over a no-increase rate of 17.005 mills. Check your current bill with the tax commissioner for the rate in force.

Who owes the tax if my Dooly County house sells midyear?

The person who owned it January 1 is liable for the full year under Georgia law. A contract can pass part to the buyer, so check the proration on the closing statement.
